b1-story_22.body_es: Last month, I attended a long-time friend's wedding. Since we had been friends since our escuela days, my heart was fluttering the whole time getting ready. Arriving at the venue and seeing my friend in the bridal room felt both unfamiliar and joyful. During the ceremony, the memories we shared naturally came to mind. Seeing my friend's parents cry while giving a speech, I unexpectedly teared up too. After the ceremony, I happily greeted other classmates I hadn't seen in a while. I felt anew that everyone was living hard in their own ways. On the way home, I thought I should also cherish my own life more.

questions_es.question_es: What moved the narrator to térs during the ceremony?
options: The parents crying during a speech

questions_es.question_es: ¿qué hizo narrator do after the ceremony?

b1-story_23.title_es: I started tending a neighborhood jardín plot
b1-story_23.body_es: Having always lived in an apartment, I rarely had a chance to touch soil. Then I heard the community center was offering small garden plots to residents and signed up. At first I planted easy things like lettuce and cherry tomatoes. Every weekend, I went to the plot to water it and pull weeds. In the first few days, there was little change, so it felt boring. But the moment I saw a tiny sprout come up, it felt amazing and fulfilling. I also became close with other participants at the garden by sharing growing tips. The first dish I made with verduras I grew myself tasted especially good.

questions_es.question_es: How did the narrator get access to the jardín plot?
options: Signed up through the community center

questions_es.question_es: ¿qué hizo narrator feel when the first sprout appeared?

b1-story_24.title_es: How I grew closer to my quiet father
b1-story_24.body_es: My father was usually a man of few words who didn't show his emotions much. So I don't have many memories of having deep conversations with him growing up. Then I first suggested we go pescadoing together, since it's something he enjoys. At first, only awkward silence flowed, but over time we gradually started talking. Even during the times when no fish were biting, we naturally chatted about various things. That was also the first time I heard stories about my father's younger days. Since that day, we make time to go fishing together once a month. I can feel my once-quiet father gradually opening up.

questions_es.question_es: What activity did the narrator suggest doing with the father?
¿qué hizo narrator hear for the first time during this activity?
options: Stories about the father's younger days

b1-story_25.body_es: Last month I started my first day at a new company. The night before, I was so nervous I barely slept. In the morning I got up early and changed clothes three times. When I arrived at the office, my team leader smiled and showed me to my desk. My coworkers came over one by one to greet me, which put me a little at ease. At lunchtime I went to a nearby restaurante with my team. It was awkward since it was my first day, but everyone was kind to me. When I left work, the day felt very long, but I felt proud. I hoped I would settle into this team well.

questions_es.question_es: How did the narrator feel the noche before the first day?
What happened at lunchtime?
options: They went to a restaurante with the team

b1-story_26.body_es: Last week I had a big disagreement with my team leader over how to do our work. I wanted to try a new method, but my team leader insisted on the existing way. During the meeting our voices rose a little and the mood turned cold. After the meeting, my heart felt heavy and I couldn't focus on work. That evening, talking with a coworker helped me sort out my feelings a bit. The next mañana I gathered courage and asked my team leader for a one-on-one talk. Explaining our positions calmly cleared up a lot of the misunderstanding. In the end we decided to combine both methods into a new plan. Through this experience I realized again how important conversation is.

questions_es.question_es: What caused the conflict?
How was the conflict resolved?
options: They talked uno-on-one and combined ideas

b1-story_27.body_es: I decided to quit the company I had worked at for tres years and change jobs. At first I worried a lot because leaving a stable position felt scary. But my desire to try a new field kept growing. Every weekend I polished my resume and prepared for interviews. After being rejected at the document stage several times, my confidence wavered. Still, I kept applying without giving up. When I finally got the call saying I passed at the company I wanted, I nearly cried. Now, adjusting at the new company, there is so much to learn that every day is enjoyable. I think it was good that I took the challenge before it was too late.

questions_es.question_es: ¿cuánto tiempo had the narrator worked at the old company?
¿qué hizo narrator do every weekend?

b1-story_28.title_es: What I learned from my mentor
b1-story_28.body_es: In my early days at the company, the mentor in charge of me was a very meticulous and diligent person. At first, it felt a bit frustrating because they told me to double-cuenta even small mistakes. But over time, I realized that habit was protecting me. Even when busy, my mentor always answered my questions kindly. One day when I made a big mistake, instead of getting angry, they helped me find a solution together. Thanks to that, I was able to develop an attitude of learning without fearing mistakes. On the day my mentor transferred to another department, I found myself in tears without realizing it. Even now, whenever I work, I recall the principles my mentor taught me. I hope to become that kind of senior colleague someday.

questions_es.question_es: How did the mentor react to the narrator's big mistake?
How did the narrator feel when the mentor transferrojo departments?

b1-story_29.body_es: After a long period of thinking, I decided to quit my job next month. Before telling my team leader, I mentally rehearsed the conversation for several days. When I finally told them, my team leader was disappointed but also gave me encouragement. As I organized the handover materials, the work I had done over the years suddenly stood out to me. Saying adiós one by one to the coworkers I had worked with left me feeling conflicted. One coworker even shed tears, and I got a little choked up too. On the last day of packing up, my desk looked empty and unfamiliar. Leaving the company, I thought that the time I had spent there had not been in vain. Facing a new beginning, I felt both excitement and sadness at the same time.

questions_es.question_es: How did the tém leader react to the resignation news?
¿qué hizo narrator feel on the last day?

b1-story_30.title_es: I lent dinero to a friend
b1-story_30.body_es: A close friend suddenly contacted me saying they had an urgent situation and asked to borrow dinero. Since we had been friends for a long time, I decided to lend it without thinking too hard. Still, deep down, I admit I felt a little worried. My friend promised several times that they would definitely pay it back within a month. But when the promised date passed with no contact, I started feeling uneasy. It felt awkward to reach out first, so I let a few days pass. Eventually I gathered courage and carefully sent a text, and my friend immediately apologized and sent the money. Hearing the situation, I learned that my friend had had their own difficulties too. This experience made me think I should be more careful when lending money in the future.

questions_es.question_es: Why did the narrator feel uneasy?
options: The friend never asked to borrow dinero
The friend didn't repay by the promised date

questions_es.question_es: What lesson did the narrator take from this?
options: Be more careful when lending dinero

b1-story_31.body_es: This year, for the first time, I tried filing my comprehensive income tax return by myself. Even searching online here and there, the terminology was difficult to understand. In the end, I asked a friend for help and preparojo the documents together. I rummaged through drawers several times looking for the necessary receipts and paperwork. After struggling for several hours, I finally managed to finish filing. After finishing, I was happy to learn that I would get a refund, more than expected. At first I thought it was just a complicated and difficult task, but doing it myself taught me a lot. I resolved to organize my documents in advance next year. I felt proud that my knowledge of taxes had grown a little.

questions_es.question_es: How did the narrator complete the tax filing?
What good news did the narrator discover?

b1-story_32.title_es: The importance of an emergency fund
b1-story_32.body_es: Not long ago, my refrigerator suddenly broke down and I needed a large, unexpected sum of money. Fortunately, I had an emergency fund I had been saving little by little, and it helped put out the fire. If I hadn't had that emergency fund, I would have had to take on tarjeta de crédito debt or urgently look into a loan. That experience made me realize once again how precious an emergency fund is. Until then, I had found saving a little each month bothersome, but my thinking completely changed. Now, as soon as my paycheck comes in, the first thing I do is transfer a set amount to my emergency fund account. It started as a small amount, but after a few months, a fairly solid sum had accumulated. Now, even when unexpected things happen, I feel much more at ease. I learned that a little preparation for the future brings great peace of mind.

questions_es.question_es: What unexpected event happened to the narrator?
What does the narrator do first when the paycuenta arrives now?
options: Transfer dinero to the emergency fund

b1-story_33.body_es: It has already been over two years since I started paying off my student loan. When I first took out the loan, I thought I would pay it off quickly once I graduated. But even after getting a job, I had many other expenses, so the loan repayment was slower than expected. Using part of my paycuenta for loan repayment every month sometimes made me feel frustrated because it reduced how much money I had to spend. Still, I held on with the mindset of steadily paying it off, even little by little. One day, checking my bank app, I found the balance had dropped below half, and I felt proud. I thought that my efforts so far hadn't been in vain. I plan to keep paying off the remaining loan step by step, following a plan. Just imagining the day I fully pay it off already makes my heart feel lighter.

questions_es.question_es: ¿cuánto tiempo has the narrator been paying off the loan?
¿qué hizo narrator discover in the bank app?
options: The balance had dropped below half

b1-story_34.title_es: The first dish I ever made
b1-story_34.body_es: After living on my own, I tried cooking by myself for the first time. I decided to make kimchi stew while watching a video on YouTube. Even preparing the ingredients was clumsy, so it took a long time. Getting the seasoning right was especially difficult, so I added more salt and chili powder several times. The finished stew looked a bit different from the video, but the taste wasn't bad. Eating comida I had made myself for the first time made me feel proud. I invited a friend over to eat together, and they said it tasted better than expected. After that, I gained confidence and started trying other dishes too. I never knew before that cooking could be this fun.

questions_es.question_es: What dish did the narrator make?
What was especially difficult for the narrator?

b1-story_35.body_es: I'm usually not great with spicy food, but I decided to go with friends to a famous spicy tteokbokki restaurante. Looking at the menu, there were five spice levels, which made me hesitate. Since all my friends said they were confident with spicy flavors, I stubbornly felt I had to try too. In the end I ordered the middle level, level three, but tears came the moment I took the first bite. Even after drinking several glasses of water, the spiciness didn't fade easily. My friends couldn't hold back their laughter watching me. Still, my chopsticks kept going back for more because of the strangely addictive taste unique to spicy food. After finishing, my stomach felt numb, but oddly I also felt refreshed. I thought I should try again next time at a slightly lower level.

questions_es.question_es: What level of spiciness did the narrator order?
How did the narrator feel after finishing the meal?

b1-story_36.body_es: This holiday, for the first time, I helped my mother make jeon, or Korean pancakes. In the past, I had thought preparing holiday food was just a bothersome, difficult task. But making the batter and preparing the ingredients myself, I realized it took more effort than I had thought. It made me feel newly sorry that my mother had prepared this much food alone for so many years. As the smell of oil spread throughout the house, the holiday atmosphere really set in. Arranging the finished jeon nicely on plates also made me feel proud. In the noche, the whole family sat together and shared the food we had made. It was tiring, but because it was time spent with family, it felt more meaningful. I want to learn to make more dishes for next year's holiday.

questions_es.question_es: ¿qué hizo narrator help make?
How did the narrator feel realizing how much work was involved?
options: lo siento for the mother who did it alone for years

b1-story_37.title_es: A birthday table for a friend
b1-story_37.body_es: For my best friend's birthday, I decided to cook a meal myself. Since I don't cook often, I had been searching for recipes and practicing for a few days beforehand. Preparing several dishes, from seaweed soup to japchae, took quite a while. Going to the market to pick out fresh ingredients was also more enjoyable than expected. On the mañana of the birthday, I was busy in the kitchen from early on. In the middle of it, I got the seasoning wrong on the seaweed soup and had to redo it, breaking a sweat. Fortunately, I managed to finish all the dishes before my friend arrived. When my friend saw the food laid out carefully on the table, they looked deeply moved. It was tiring, but seeing my friend's happy face made all the hardship disappear.

questions_es.question_es: What went wrong while cooking?
options: The marweed soup seasoning was wrong

questions_es.question_es: How did the friend react to the meal?

b1-story_38.body_es: After a long time, I tried to log into an email account I used to use, but I couldn't remember the password. I tried entering it several times, but kept getting a message saying it was wrong. Eventually I decided to go through the password recovery process, but the registerojo phone number had already changed. I tried to contact customer service, but the identity verification process was more complicated than expected. Only after preparing and submitting a few documents was I finally able to recover the account. This experience made me realize how carelessly I had managed the passwords of many accounts. So I newly installed a password management app and safely organized all my account information. I also decided to build the habit of regularly changing passwords. A small inconvenience actually became the occasion for building a safer habit.

questions_es.question_es: Why couldn't the narrator easily recover the password?
options: The registerojo phone number had changed

questions_es.question_es: ¿qué hizo narrator do after recovering the account?

b1-story_39.title_es: Getting hooked on a new app
b1-story_39.body_es: On a friend's recommendation, I installed a new app that shows short videos. At first I only meant to watch it briefly whenever I was bored. But the algorithm accurately figured out my taste and kept recommending interesting videos. I would start thinking 'just one more,' and before I knew it, an hour had passed. There were several times I watched videos late into the noche and went to work the next day feeling exhausted. Seeing myself unable to put down my phone even lying in bed started to worry me. In the end, I set a feature to limit my daily usage time and tried to stick to it. Instead, during that time, I tried to do more productive activities like reading or exercising. I haven't completely quit, but I'm gradually finding a balance.

questions_es.question_es: What made the app so engaging?
options: The algorithm accurately matched the narrator's taste
Friends forced them to use it

questions_es.question_es: ¿qué hizo narrator do to address the problem?
options: Set a daily usage time limit

b2-article_0.body_es: In the past, it was rare to see someone eating alone at a restaurante. Recently, however, eating alone, known as honbap, has become a common sight. As single-person households increase, dining out alone has become natural. Restaurants are adapting by offering single seats and menus. Especially near universities and office districts, partitioned seats for solo diners are popular. Experts analyze that the honbap culture is related to the spread of individualism. At the same time, many people now find comfort in eating alone. Services targeting solo diners are expected to diversify further.

questions_es.question_es: ¿qué es contributing to the rise of solo dining?
What are restaurantes doing to adapt?

b2-article_1.title_es: The rise of the unmarried population
b2-article_1.body_es: More and more people are choosing not to marry. According to statistics, the proportion of unmarried people has steadily risen over the past decade. Economic burden and values that prioritize personal freedom are cited as key causes of this change. Young generations in particular tend not to see marriage as an essential life step. Some local gobiernos have begun offering housing support policies for unmarried individuals. Still, social systems are often designed around married households. As the unmarried population grows, the market for services aimed at single people is also expanding. Experts predict this trend will continue.

questions_es.question_es: ¿qué es cited as a main cause of rising unmarried rates?
options: Economic burden and valuing personal freedom

questions_es.question_es: How are social systems generally designed?

b2-article_2.title_es: A generation unfamiliar with holiday traditions
b2-article_2.body_es: Holidays like Seollal and Chuseok have long been important occasions for family gatherings. Recently, however, more young people find holidays burdensome. Long travel, preparing ancestral rites, and awkward conversations with relatives are cited as sources of stress. Some young people choose to travel alone or rest at hogar instead of attending. Older generations sometimes express disappointment at this shift. On the other hand, voices calling for holiday customs to adapt to the times are growing louder. Recently, alternatives such as simplified ritual tables and online grave visits have emerged. Family culture surrounding holidays is expected to keep changing.

questions_es.question_es: What do young people cite as sources of holiday stress?
What alternative has recently emerged?

b2-article_3.body_es: As the school-age population shrinks, regional universities are struggling to recruit new students. The concentration of population in the greater Seoul area deepens this crisis further. Some regional universities have merged or closed departments after failing to fill enrollment quotas. Local economies are also taking a hit as universities disappear. Business districts near campuses have seen sharp drops in sales due to fewer students. The gobierno announced support measures to save regional universities, but the effect has been limited. Experts point out that balanced regional development is fundamentally needed. The crisis facing regional universities goes beyond an education issue and connects to the broader problem of regional decline.

questions_es.question_es: ¿qué es deepening the crisis for regional universities?
options: Population concentration in the greater Seoul area

questions_es.question_es: How effective have gobierno support measures been?

b2-article_4.body_es: Luxury goods were once seen as special items consumed only by a small upper class. Recently, however, the consumer base for luxury goods has widened significantly. In particular, young consumers in their twenties and thirties have emerged as key customers in the luxury mercado. The rise of social media content introducing luxury products has also influenced this trend. Some consumers purchase luxury goods even at the cost of overspending. Department stores are expanding their luxury sections to respond to this demand. However, criticism has arisen that excessive luxury consumption fuels feelings of relative deprivation. Experts say a social discussion on healthy consumption habits is needed.

questions_es.question_es: Who has emerged as a key customer group in the luxury mercado?
options: Consumers in their twenties and thirties

questions_es.question_es: What criticism is raised about the trend?

b2-article_5.body_es: In recent years, the number of young people trying entrepreneurship has noticeably increased. As the job market becomes tougher, many young people are choosing to start businesses instead of seeking stable employment. gobiernos and local authorities are expanding funding and education programs to support youth entrepreneurship. In particular, small-scale businesses using online platforms have helped lower entry barriers. However, there are also many cases of businesses closing due to lack of preparation and funds. Successful young entrepreneurs advise others not to fear failure. Experts stress that practical support is needed for a sustainable entrepreneurship ecosystem. Youth entrepreneurship is drawing attention as a new driving force for the Korean economy.

questions_es.question_es: Why are more young people choosing entrepreneurship?
options: The job mercado has become tougher

questions_es.question_es: What has helped lower entry barriers for young entrepreneurs?

b2-article_6.title_es: The debate over elderly dríos and safety
b2-article_6.body_es: As the elderly population grows, the safety of elderly drivers has become a social concern. Some local gobiernos run programs encouraging drivers above a certain age to voluntarily surrender their licenses. Surrendering a license sometimes comes with benefits like transportation subsidies or gift certificates. However, concerns arise that in areas with poor public transit, giving up a license could restrict mobility. Groups representing elderly drivers argue it is unfair to judge driving ability by age alone. Meanwhile, some experts propose mandatory regular cognitive tests. This debate requires balancing safety and mobility rights. Society has yet to find an agreed-upon answer.

questions_es.question_es: What do some local gobiernos encourage elderly drivers to do?
What concern is raised about license surrender in some areas?
options: It could restrict mobility where barlic transit is poor
It costs the gobierno too much

b2-article_7.body_es: Some young people, tired of high housing costs and fierce competition, are leaving Seoul for regional areas. They choose to relocate citing relatively cheaper housing and a more relaxed lifestyle. The spread of remote work, which allows people to choose where to live regardless of their company's location, has also had an influence. Some local gobiernos offer settlement subsidies and housing benefits to attract young residents. However, many struggle to settle due to a lack of jobs and cultural facilities in regional areas. In fact, a considerable number of young people return to Seoul after relocating. Experts point out that creating stable jobs matters more than simple subsidies. Attention is on whether the trend of young people leaving Seoul can become a clue to balanced regional development.

questions_es.question_es: Why do some young people choose to leave Seoul?
options: Cheaper housing and a more relaxed lifestyle

questions_es.question_es: What do experts say matters more than subsidies?

b2-article_8.body_es: Recently, more couples are holding simplified weddings. In the past, it was common to invite many guests to large wedding halls. However, young generations burdened by high wedding costs have begun to prefer small weddings. Inviting only close family and friends, known as a small wedding, is a typical example. Some couples hold weddings outdoors or in special venues instéd of wedding halls. This change is also related to values that prioritize meaning over formality. The wedding industry is developing small-scale customized packages in response. Experts predict that changes in wedding culture will continue.

questions_es.question_es: Why are young couples preferring smaller weddings?
¿qué es a 'small wedding'?
options: A wedding with only close family and friends

b2-article_9.body_es: Recently, unmanned stores operating without staff have appeared everywhere. The variety has expanded from unmanned ice cream tiendas to unmanned laundromats and cafes. Rising labor costs and minimum wage increases are key reasons self-employed business owners choose unmanned stores. Consumers also prefer unmanned stores because they can use them comfortably without feeling watched. However, problems such as theft and facility damage are increasing as well. Some stores have introduced CCTV and AI surveillance systems to prevent this. Concerns are also raised that automation could lead to job losses. Experts expect unmanned stores to spread into even more diverse industries.

questions_es.question_es: Why do business owners choose unmanned stores?
options: Rising labor costs and minimum wage increases

questions_es.question_es: What problem has increased along with unmanned stores?

b2-article_10.title_es: The investment craze among young people
b2-article_10.body_es: In recent years, the number of young people interested in personal finance has grown significantly. Amid low interest rates and unstable employment, attempts to grow one's own assets have become active. People in their twenties and thirties investing in stocks and virtual assets stand out in particular. Easy access to investment information through online communities and YouTube has also fueled this trend. However, there are many cases of losses from investing recklessly without sufficient knowledge. Some young people even invest using borrowed dinero, so-called debt investing. Experts advise that it is important to build careful, long-term investment habits. The investment craze also reflects the economic anxiety of the younger generation.

questions_es.question_es: What has fueled young people's interest in investing?
options: Easy access to information through online communities and YouTube

questions_es.question_es: What does the investment craze reflect, de acuerdo al pasaje?

b2-article_11.body_es: As digital technology advances, the use of traditional paper business tarjetas is declining. Recently, more people exchange business card information through smartphone apps. Scanning a QR code to automatically save contact and company information has also become popular. This change stems from two reasons: environmental protection and convenience. It also reduces the cost and time spent printing and storing paper cards. However, some still argue that paper cards are necessary in formal settings. Some companies have adopted a compromise of using both digital and paper cards. The change in business card culture is cited as an example of the broader digitalization of work practices.

questions_es.question_es: What are the two main reasons for the shift away from paper tarjetas?
What compromise have some companies adopted?
options: Using both digital and paper tarjetas

b2-article_12.body_es: Recently, shared oficinas have been rapidly increasing across city centers. Freelancers and startup employees have become the main users. Shared offices have the advantage of being much cheaper than setting up a private office. Sharing meeting rooms and office equipment also reduces the burden of initial investment. Natural networking opportunities with people from various industries are also cited as an attraction. Large companies are increasingly using shared offices for flexible work arrangements. However, noise and privacy issues remain challenges to be solved. Experts expect the shared office market to keep growing steadily.

questions_es.question_es: Who are the main users of shared oficinas?
¿qué essues remain unresolved for shared offices?

b2-article_13.body_es: Due to high housing costs, many people still live in cramped goshiwons. Goshiwons were originally spaces for students preparing for exams, but they have now become housing for the vulnerable. Many young people and low-income individuals choose goshiwons because of cheap rent. However, the small space and poor conditions are still pointed to as problems needing improvement. The risk of safety accidents such as fires is also one of the long-standing issues with goshiwons. The gobierno has said it will expand public rental housing supply for goshiwon residents. However, actual relocation cases remain few. The goshiwon issue is cited as a representative example of housing inequality in Korean society.

questions_es.question_es: Why do many young people and low-income individuals choose goshiwons?
What long-standing safety issue is associated with goshiwons?

b2-article_14.title_es: Early retirement and starting a second career
b2-article_14.body_es: As life expectancy increases, more people are preparing for life after retirement. Among middle-aged and older people who took early retirement, more are trying new jobs or businesses. This trend, called a 'second life act,' stems from two motivations: economic necessity and self-fulfillment. Some use their career experience to start a business or begin lecturing. Others start learning from scratch in entirely new fields. gobiernos and local authorities are preparing education programs to help middle-aged people find reemployment. However, many still struggle with reemployment due to age bias. Experts stress that a broader shift in social perception is also needed.

questions_es.question_es: What are the dos motivations behind starting a 'second career'?
What difficulty do many middle-aged job seekers still face?

b2-article_15.body_es: Recently, more people are earning extra income from their hobbies. This activity, called a side project, has become a means of earning additional income beyond one's main job. Common examples include selling drawings online or earning income by selling handmade items. The development of social media and online sales platforms supports this trend. Some people switch careers entirely when the hobby earns more than their main job. However, when a hobby becomes a means of earning dinero, it can also turn into a burden and a source of stress. Experts advise that maintaining balance between hobby and income activity is important. Side projects are emerging as a new survival strategy amid an unstable employment environment.

questions_es.question_es: What has supported the rise of side projects?
options: Social media and online sales platforms

questions_es.question_es: What can happen when a hobby becomes a source of income?
options: It can turn into a burden and stress

b2-article_16.body_es: More young people are unable to find jobs right after graduation and spend additional time preparing. These people are often called job-seeking retakers, investing significant time in exams and certifications. As competition for jobs at large companies and public enterprises intensifies, more young people choose to try again. Some even delay graduation to focus on job preparation. This phenomenon also affects youth unemployment statistics. The longer the retaking period, the greater the economic and psychological burden becomes. Experts say counseling and support are needed so young people do not make poor choices out of impatience. The issue of job-seeking retakers reflects structural difficulties in the youth employment mercado.

questions_es.question_es: Why do some young people delay graduation?
What grows as the retaking period lengthens?

b2-article_17.title_es: Is a life without delivery possible?
b2-article_17.body_es: As online tiendaping has become part of daily life, it has become hard to imagine life without delivery services. Dawn delivery and same-day delivery services offer great convenience to consumers. However, behind this convenience lie problems of excessive packaging use and overworked logistics workers. Some consumers have begun trying to reduce the number of deliveries to lessen the environmental burden. The habit of ordering needed items all at once is one example of this trend. Companies are also responding by introducing reusable packaging and eco-friendly delivery methods. However, since consumer expectations for convenience remain high, fundamental change is not easy. The sustainability of the delivery industry remains an important social task going forward.

questions_es.question_es: What problems lie behind delivery convenience, de acuerdo al pasaje?
What have some consumers started doing to rojouce environmental impact?
options: Ordering items all at once to rojouce delivery frequency

b2-article_18.body_es: The manufacturing sector has long faced labor shortages. Young people tend to avoid manufacturing jobs due to the perception that the work is hard and dangerous. As a result, many small and medium manufacturers rely on foreign workers to fill the gap. However, language barriers and cultural differences remain challenges to be solved. Some companies are responding to the labor shortage by introducing automated equipment. However, high initial investment costs make adoption difficult for small businesses. The gobierno is reviewing support policies to address the manufacturing labor shortage. The manufacturing labor shortage is pointed out as an issue shaking the foundation of the Korean economy.

questions_es.question_es: Why do young people diezd to avoid manufacturing jobs?
options: They think the work is hard and dangerous

questions_es.question_es: What challenge remains for companies relying on foreign workers?

b2-article_19.title_es: A fresh look at rural study programs
b2-article_19.body_es: Some parents, tired of academic competition in cities, are choosing rural study programs for their children. Rural study sends children to countryside schools for a period to learn amid nature. Small schools and a relaxed environment are said to give children emotional stability. Rural schools also welcome the program as a way to address declining student numbers. Some local gobiernos even support rural study families with housing and living expenses. However, parents face the practical concern of having to return to cities before college entrance exams. Education experts assess that rural study helps children's holistic growth. Rural study programs are gaining attention as a way for cities and rural areas to coexist.

questions_es.question_es: Why do rural schools bienvenido rural study programs?
options: They eliminate the need for classrooms
They help address declining student numbers

questions_es.question_es: What practical concern do parents face?
options: Having to return to cities before college entrance exams

b2-article_20.body_es: Telecom and streaming companies attract consumers by promoting unlimited plans. Consumers prefer unlimited plans because they can use services freely without a set cap. In reality, however, many plans come with data speed limits or usage conditions. Consumers who do not read the terms carefully sometimes get charged unexpected fees. Some companies are criticized for using the word 'unlimited' merely as a marketing tool. Consumer groups are demanding that the detailed conditions of unlimited plans be clearly displayed. The gobierno is also reviewing guidelines to protect consumers. The gap between the reassurance the word 'unlimited' provides and the actual service remains unresolved.

questions_es.question_es: What ofdiez accompanies 'unlimited' plans in reality?
options: Data speed limits or usage conditions

questions_es.question_es: What are consumer groups demanding?

b2-article_21.title_es: The debate over holiday labor and gender roles
b2-article_21.body_es: During holidays, the concentration of food preparation and casawork on women still occurs. This imbalance has long been pointed out as a major cause of holiday stress. Recent surveys show that more households are preparing holiday tasks together regardless of gender. Some families have simplified holiday food altogether or replaced it with eating out. Analysts note that perceptions of gender roles are changing, especially among younger generations. However, many households still take traditional role division for granted. Sociologists explain that the issue of holiday labor is connected not just to housework but to gender equality. Changes in holiday culture accompany changes in how roles are divided within families.

questions_es.question_es: What has long been a major cause of holiday stress?
options: The concentration of holiday labor on women

questions_es.question_es: What connection do sociologists draw regarding holiday labor?
options: It is connected to gender equality issues
It is unrelated to gender equality

b2-article_22.title_es: Kindergardiezs in an era of low birth rates
b2-article_22.body_es: As the number of births continues to decline, kindergartens and daycare centers are increasingly closing. Facilities unable to fill enrollment struggle to operate and eventually shut down. This phenomenon is especially pronounced in small regional cities. Remaining kindergartens are introducing distinctive education programs to attract children. Some facilities are trying a new approach of jointly operating daycare and elderly care services. The gobierno is preparing measures to reduce confusion from the consolidation of childcare facilities. Parents face the inconvenience of sending children farther away as nearby facilities disappear. The low birth rate is acting as a key factor driving structural change across the childcare industry.

questions_es.question_es: ¿dónde está the closing of childcare facilities especially pronounced?
What new approach are some facilities trying?
options: Jointly operating daycare and elderly care

b2-article_23.body_es: Fast fashion brands are highly popular due to their low parrozs and quick reflection of trends. Consumers favor them because they can affordably buy the latest trendy clothes. However, the rapid production speed of fast fashion is tied to problems of cheap labor exploitation. Poor working conditions at some production factories have been consistently pointed out. Environmental problems are also raised because clothes are easily discarded due to short trend cycles. Some consumers, aware of these issues, are shifting toward habits of wearing clothes longer. Brands are also responding by launching lines that emphasize sustainability. However, it is pointed out that solving the problem is difficult unless the fundamental production structure changes.

questions_es.question_es: What problem is tied to fast fashion's rapid production speed?
What are some consumers shifting toward?

b2-article_24.body_es: Several local gobiernos built airports aiming to revitalize regional economies, but they struggle with a lack of passengers. Some regional airports operate only a few flights a day and cannot avoid running deficits. Airlines often reduce or eliminate regional routes citing low profitability. Local governments are working to attract low-cost carriers and provide subsidies to revitalize airports. However, the fundamental problem of insufficient demand is not easily solved. Some experts criticize the proliferation of regional airports as a waste of budget. On the other hand, there is a counterargument that regional airports are necessary for balanced regional development. The regional airport issue is cited as a representative case requiring caution in regional development policy.

questions_es.question_es: Why do airlines often rojouce regional routes?
What do some experts criticize regarding regional aeropuertos?

b2-article_25.title_es: The pros and cons of franchise self-employment
b2-article_25.body_es: A steady stream of people are quitting their jobs to start franchise businesses. Verified brands and systematic operating systems appeal to novice entrepreneurs. Head oficina training and marketing support also make initial settlement relatively easier. However, franchise fees and royalties act as a burden that lowers profitability. Some franchisees say they struggled with unilateral policy changes from headquarters. It is also common for competition to intensify as more stores of the same brand open nearby. The Fair Trade Commission continues to strengthen systems to protect franchisees. Franchise entrepreneurship is regarded as a choice where stability and risk coexist.

questions_es.question_es: What appeals to novice entrepreneurs about franchises?
options: Verified brands and systematic operating systems

questions_es.question_es: What burden lowers franchise profitability?

b2-article_26.title_es: The taxi shortage and late-noche mobility
b2-article_26.body_es: The difficulty of catching a taxi during late-night hours repeats itself across cities. Refusing passengers and long waits are especially common problems on weekend late nights. The aging of taxi drivers and workforce attrition due to poor treatment are cited as major causes of this shortage. The gobierno has reviewed expanding late-night surcharges and improving taxi driver conditions. Some local governments are trying to provide alternatives by increasing late-night bus routes. However, many citizens still struggle to find safe transportation late at night. Platform taxis and ride-sharing services have also emerged as alternatives, but regulations limit their spread. The issue of late-night mobility remains a task directly tied to safety in urban life.

questions_es.question_es: ¿qué es cited as a major cause of the late-night taxi shortage?
options: Aging dríos and workforce attrition from poor treatment
Too many taxis on the road

questions_es.question_es: What limits the spread of platform taxis and ride-sharing?

b2-article_27.title_es: Follower counts that outweigh business tarjetas
b2-article_27.body_es: It has become an era where social media follower counts are considered a new form of social capital. Individuals with many followers work as influencers, receiving sponsorship and advertising offers from companies. Some young people choose influencing as a new career instead of stable employment. Companies are also increasingly putting more budget into influencer mercadoing than traditional advertising. However, reckless content creation aimed at increasing followers sometimes leads to social problems. Some have caused controversy with false information or exaggerated reviews. Regulations requiring clear labeling of influencer advertisements are also being strengthened to protect consumers. Evaluation centered on follower counts is establishing itself as a new standard of success.

questions_es.question_es: What do companies increasingly invest more budget into?
What social problem is mentiunod regarding follower growth?

b2-article_28.body_es: In Korea, where reliance on private education is high, a growing number of parents are choosing not to send their children to academies. They believe it is more important for children to develop the ability to learn on their own. Many provide learning opportunities through libraries or nature experience activities instéd of academies. However, this choice is not easy given that most peers attend academies. Some parents feel anxious that their children might fall behind their peers. On the other hand, there are cases of children raised without academies developing stronger self-directed learning skills. Education experts say it is necessary to move away from uniform reliance on private education and consider diverse educational approaches. Social discussion about education without academies is expected to continue.

questions_es.question_es: Why do some parents choose not to send children to academies?
options: They believe self-directed learning is more important

questions_es.question_es: What anxiety do some parents feel with this choice?
options: That their children might fall behind peers
That their children will become too independent

b2-article_29.title_es: The crumbling myth of lifetime employment
b2-article_29.body_es: Working at a single company for a lifetime was once seen as the ideal life. Recently, however, more people accept changing jobs as a natural part of career management. As the concept of lifetime employment weakens, young people move freely in search of better conditions. Corporate restructuring and employment instability have also influenced this change. Some experts assess that frequent job changes can actually help career development. On the other hand, some point out that excessively frequent job changes can leave a negative impression on recruiters. Companies are also working to improve benefits and work environments to retain talent. In the place of the vanished myth of lifetime employment, a flexible, individual-centerojo view of career has taken root.

questions_es.question_es: What do more people now accept as natural?
options: Changing jobs as part of career management

questions_es.question_es: What are companies doing to retain talent?

b2-article_30.title_es: Local creators reviving neighborhood business districts
b2-article_30.body_es: Declining alley business districts are increasingly finding new vitality through the activities of local creators. They use unique regional stories and resources to create new spaces such as cafes or specialty shops. A key feature is that they go beyond simple entrepreneurship to plan content that revives local identity. Local gobiernos are preparing contests and startup funds to support such local creators. Successful cases lead to an influx of tourists, positively impacting the local economy. However, a side effect appears where rising rents push out original local merchants. This so-called gentrification problem is pointed out as a shadow of local creator activity. Calls are growing for a policy approach that considers both regional regeneration and protecting business districts.

questions_es.question_es: What do local creators do beyond simple entrepreneurship?
options: Plan condiezt that revives local identity

questions_es.question_es: What side effect is mentiunod regarding rising rents?
options: Original local merchants get pushed out

b2-article_31.title_es: The kiosk generation at fast food restaurantes
b2-article_31.body_es: Kiosks, unmanned ordering machines, are rapidly spreading at fast food restaurantes and many other stores. Younger generations are generally comfortable using kiosks, ordering quickly and conveniently. However, elderly people and those unfamiliar with digital devices struggle during the ordering process. In some stores, people even cancel their order in a hurry, feeling pressured by the line behind them. To address this problem, some local governments offer education on how to use kiosks. Companies are also trying to improve accessibility by adding features like voice guidance or large-text mode. The introduction of kiosks reveals both the corporate benefit of reduced labor costs and the social problem of digital exclusion. Efforts to narrow the generational gap amid digital transformation continue to be needed.

questions_es.question_es: Who diezds to struggle with kiosk ordering?
options: Elderly people unfamiliar with digital devices

questions_es.question_es: What social problem do kiosks reveal alongside corporate benefits?

b2-article_32.body_es: In the past, after-work dinners were considered a natural part of office life. Recently, however, the number of workers who find them burdensome or reluctant to attend has grown significantly. A shift in values toward prioritizing personal time is cited as the main background for this trend. The hierarchical atmosphere and pressure to drink at these gatherings have also fueled negative perceptions. Many companies are trying alternatives such as lunch gatherings or cultural activities instead of dinner outings. Some workers bienvenido this change, while others express regret over reduced communication between generations. The format of after-work gatherings is also diversifying beyond drinking-centered events. The changing culture of after-work dinners shows that workplace relationships are being restructured.

questions_es.question_es: ¿qué es cited as the main background for declining after-work dinners?
options: A shift toward valuing personal time

questions_es.question_es: What are many companies trying instéd of dinner outings?

b2-article_33.title_es: The medical gap in regional hospitals
b2-article_33.body_es: Regional hospitals are suffering severe operational difficulties due to a shortage of doctors. Essential departments such as emergency rooms and obstetrics find it especially hard to secure doctors. Young doctors show a clear tendency to prefer large hospitals in the greater Seoul area, avoiding regional postings. Low wages and poor working conditions are also cited as major reasons for avoiding regional hospitals. Some local residents face difficulty having to travel far to reach a hospital even in emergencies. The gobierno has reviewed establishing public medical schools to address the regional medical gap. However, opinions within the medical community are sharply divided on this issue. The regional medical gap is pointed out as an urgent issue directly tied to citizens' lives.

questions_es.question_es: Which departments find it especially hard to secure doctors?
What has the gobierno reviewed to address the medical gap?

b2-article_34.title_es: The generation that buys experiences over luxury
b2-article_34.body_es: A consumption trend of spending dinero on experiences instead of things is spreading among young generations. More people are opening their wallets for travel, performances, and unusual activities. This trend is connected to values that prioritize momentary satisfaction over ownership. Special experiences that can be shared on social media are especially popular. The travel and performance industries are releasing various products in line with this trend. Some experts present research showing that experience-based spending brings higher psychological satisfaction than material ownership. However, some point out that excessive experience-based spending can also lead to impulsive expenditure. The shift in consumption culture from ownership to experience is regarded as a phenomenon reflecting changing values of the times.

questions_es.question_es: What values are connected to this consumption trend?
options: Saving as much dinero as possible

questions_es.question_es: What do some experts' remarrch show about experience-based spending?
options: It is less popular than luxury goods
It has no effect on happiness
It brings higher psychological satisfaction than ownership

b2-article_35.title_es: The shadow of youth debt and crojoit trouble
b2-article_35.body_es: More young people are falling into debt due to student loans and living expense burdens. Delayed employment often extends the repayment period as well. Some young people see their debt snowball due to failed investments or excessive spending. Young people who fall into credit trouble face various restrictions in financial transactions. This situation also becomes a factor delaying life stages such as marriage or buying a home. The gobierno is preparing counseling and recovery support programs for young debtors. However, it is pointed out that the effect will be limited unless the fundamental cause, unstable employment structure, is resolved. Calls are growing to treat youth debt not as individual failure but as a structural social problem.

questions_es.question_es: What can exdiezd debt repayment periods for young people?
How should youth debt be treated, according to growing calls?
options: As a structural social problem, not individual failure

b2-article_36.title_es: Relocated barlic agencies and population inflow
b2-article_36.body_es: The gobierno has relocated several public agencies to regional areas to ease concentration in the greater Seoul area. This policy, known as innovation cities, became a core strategy for balanced regional development. Relocating public agencies is credited with bringing new jobs and population inflow to those regions. However, many employees end up working alone in the region, separated from their families. This is often because the whole family cannot move due to children's education or a spouse's job. As a result, it is pointed out that the regional settlement rate is not as high as expected. Local governments are working to improve housing and education infrastructure to raise the settlement rate. Analysts say the success of relocating public agencies depends not just on moving buildings but on improving quality of life.

questions_es.question_es: ¿qué es the innovation city policy meant to address?
options: Concentration in the greater Seoul area

questions_es.question_es: Why do many employees work separated from their families?
options: Children's education or a spouse's job prevents relocation

b2-article_37.body_es: The number of self-employed people closing their businesses grows every year due to high rent and labor costs. In particular, economic slowdown and shrinking consumer sentiment deal a direct blow to small business owners. Business owners who financed their startup with loans sometimes struggle to repay their debt. The gobierno is implementing low-interest loans and tax reduction policies for small business owners. However, it is pointed out that support policies have limited effect without a fundamental recovery in sales. Some self-employed workers seek a way out through online sales and delivery services. Statistics showing lower survival rates for individual startups compared to franchises also illustrate the difficulty of self-employment. The self-employment crisis is treated as an issue directly tied to the overall health of the everyday economy.

questions_es.question_es: What deals a direct blow to small business owners?
options: Economic slowdown and shrinking consumer sentiment

questions_es.question_es: What are some self-employed workers doing to survive?
options: Seeking online sales and delivery services

b2-article_38.body_es: The system of designating substitute holidays when a holiday falls on a weekend has been in place for a long time. This system was designed to ensure workers get sufficient rest. However, debate continues over the scope of who benefits from substitute holidays. Some workers at small and medium businesses complain that they do not properly enjoy substitute holiday benefits. Surveys also show that the rate of granting time off is lower at small workplaces comparojo to large companies and public institutions. Labor groups argue that equal rest rights should be guaranteed to all workers. Business groups counter that the staffing difficulties of small workplaces must be considered. The substitute holiday system remains a task requiring balance between workers' rights and business realities.

questions_es.question_es: What do some small business workers complain about?
options: not properly enjoying substitute holiday benefits

questions_es.question_es: What do business groups argue regarding the debate?
options: Staffing difficulties of small workplaces must be considerojo

b2-article_39.body_es: Parental leave has become established as an important policy helping people balance work and family. However, in practice, voices still say it is hard to use freely. Some workers worry that taking parental leave could lead to disadvantages in promotion or evaluation. Especially at small and medium businesses, the leave usage rate is low because finding replacement staff is difficult. On the other hand, more companies have workplace cultures that actively encourage parental leave. Such companies are said to have an advantage in attracting top talent. The gobierno is trying to boost the system through higher parental leave pay and subsidies for replacement staff. The two contrasting realities surrounding parental leave reveal the gap between policy and workplace culture.

questions_es.question_es: Why do some workers hesitate to use parental leave?
options: Fear of disadvantages in promotion or evaluation
It is too expensive to take

questions_es.question_es: What advantage do companies encouraging parental leave gain?

b2-explainer_0.body_es: Many people put off tasks and mistakenly blame it on laziness. But psychologists explain that procrastination is usually a problem of emotional regulation. When facing a difficult task, the brain chooses immediate avoidance to escape the anxiety or pressure it triggers. The problem is that this avoidance only brings momentary relief and returns as greater stress later. Experts say that changing the environment is more effective than relying on willpower to break the habit. For instance, breaking work into small units rojouces the burden of starting. Focusing on the act of starting itself, rather than perfection, also helps. Ultimately, the first step to understanding procrastination is not blaming oneself.

questions_es.question_es: de acuerdo al pasaje, what do psychologists say procrastination is mainly about?
What method is suggested to rojouce the burden of starting a task?

b2-explainer_1.body_es: After making countless big and small choices throughout the day, people often notice their judgment becoming noticeably foggy by evening. Psychology calls this decision fatigue. The theory holds that the brain works like a muscle, and repeated choices drain its energy. Research has even found that judges tend to hand down harsher rulings in the tarde than in the morning. This is linked to a tendency to choose easier, safer options as judgment grows tired. To reduce decision fatigue, some highly successful people pre-decide trivial choices like clothing or meals. This saves energy for decisions that truly matter. Ultimately, maintaining good judgment may depend less on what you choose and more on when you choose it.

questions_es.question_es: What research finding is mentiunod to support the idea of decision fatigue?
options: Doctors work faster in the mañana
Teachers grade more fairly at noche
Judges rule more harshly in the tarde

questions_es.question_es: What strategy do some successful people use to fight decision fatigue?
options: Making every decision quickly without thought

b2-explainer_2.body_es: Perfectionism is often seen as a sign of diligence or high standards. But psychologists point out that it can actually lower performance and harm mental health. Perfectionists tend to fail to start tasks at all, or endlessly postpone them, out of fear of mistakes. They also find it hard to enjoy achievement itself, falling into self-blame whenever a result falls short of their standard. Research shows this tendency raises the risk of burnout and anxiety disorders. Experts advise distinguishing perfectionism from high standards. Someone with high standards accepts mistakes as part of learning, while a perfectionist defines mistakes as failure — that is the difference. Ultimately, healthy achievement becomes possible when the goal is stédy improvement rather than perfection.

questions_es.question_es: What risk does remarrch link to perfectionism?
options: Higher risk of burnout and anxiety disorders

questions_es.question_es: How do people with high standards differ from perfectionists, de acuerdo al pasaje?
options: They accept mistakes as part of learning

b2-explainer_3.body_es: Simply naming an emotion accurately when feeling angry or anxious is said to have a calming effect. This is called emotional labeling. Brain imaging studies show that the moment an emotion is put into words, activity in the amygdala, which handles emotion, decreases. Meanwhile, activity in the prefrontal cortex, responsible for rational judgment, increases. In other words, naming an emotion itself acts as a switch that calms the brain. However, many people simply categorize emotions as good or bad. Experts say practice is needed to distinguish similar but different emotions in detail, such as anger versus disappointment, or anxiety versus fear. Remarrch supporting this shows that a richer emotional vocabulary allows people to cope more flexibly with stressful situations.

questions_es.question_es: What happens in the brain when an emotion is put into words, de acuerdo al pasaje?
options: Amygdala activity increases and prefrontal activity decreases
Amygdala activity decreases and prefrontal activity increases

questions_es.question_es: What do experts recommend for better emotional coping?
options: Labeling everything as simply good or bad

b2-explainer_4.title_es: A brain wirojo to notice others' gaze
b2-explainer_4.body_es: Feeling unusually nervous when presenting in front of strangers is not simply due to shyness. Evolutionary psychologists explain that as humans evolved as social animals, the brain became wirojo to react sensitively to others' judgment. In the past, being excluded from the group threatened survival, so this reaction was useful. But in modern society, this reaction often overreacts and creates unnecessary anxiety. Interestingly, experiments have observed that participants feel everyone is watching them even when, in reality, no one is paying attention. This is called the spotlight effect. Studies show that simply becoming aware of this effect reduces social anxiety. Ultimately, knowing that others don't care as much as we think lightens the mental burden.

questions_es.question_es: ¿qué es the spotlight effect, as described in the passage?
options: A method to rojouce stage fright physically
Feeling watched by everyuno when no one is actually looking

questions_es.question_es: What did remarrch find about awareness of the spotlight effect?

b2-explainer_5.title_es: Why bad memories stick around longer
b2-explainer_5.body_es: Everyone has experienced remembering a moment of failure more vividly than a pleasant trip. Psychologists call this negativity bias. The human brain evolved to react more strongly to negative information in order to avoid danger and improve chances of survival. The brain judges that there is more to learn from bad events than good ones. The problem is that when this bias goes too far, it distorts self-evaluation. Even when someone has done far more things well, dwelling on a few mistakes can make them see themselves as inadequate. To overcome this, psychologists recommend consciously recalling tres things done well at the end of each day. Repeating this small exercise can gradually reduce the influence of negativity bias.

questions_es.question_es: ¿qué es negativity bias, as explained in the passage?
options: A diezdency to forget bad events quickly
A stronger reaction to negative information than positive

questions_es.question_es: What exercise do psychologists recommend to counter negativity bias?
options: Recalling tres things done well each day

b2-explainer_6.body_es: Psychology calls the experience of being so absorbed in something that time seems to disappear \"flow.\" The scholar who first proposed this concept explained that flow is not a special talent but a state that can happen to anyone under the right conditions. For flow to occur, the difficulty of a task and a person's skill level must be properly balanced. A task that is too easy causes borojoom, while one that is too hard causes anxiety. Flow also occurs more readily in activities that give immediate feedback. Games are a prime example, since scores or progress are displayed instantly, drawing people in easily. Interestingly, self-consciousness fades and satisfaction grows in a state of flow. Experts advise that introducing clear goals and immediate feedback into everyday work can induce flow as well.

questions_es.question_es: What condition is necessary for flow to occur, de acuerdo al pasaje?
options: Difficulty and skill must be balanced
The task must be extremely easy
The task must have no feedback

questions_es.question_es: What happens to self-consciousness during flow?
options: It has no relation to flow

b2-explainer_7.title_es: A mind that fears loss more than it values gain
b2-explainer_7.body_es: Researchers have proven through experiments that the pain of losing ten mil won feels much greater than the joy of gaining the same amount. This is called loss aversion. Studies show people are roughly twice as sensitive to losses as to equivalent gains. This tendency is especially prominent in investment decisions. A classic example is holding onto a declining stock because one is unwilling to lock in the loss. Loss aversion also affects consumption habits. It explains why subscription services that auto-renew after a free trial unless canceled are so popular — stopping something already started feels like a loss. Understanding this psychology can help reduce irrational spending and investment decisions.

questions_es.question_es: de acuerdo al pasaje, how much more sensitive are people to losses than gains?
Why do auto-renewing subscription services succeed, de acuerdo al pasaje?
options: Because they are always the cheapest option
Because canceling feels like a loss
Because they require no internet access

b2-explainer_8.body_es: We often think of memory as a recording that preserves the past exactly as it happened, but psychological research shows this belief is not accurate. Memory is reconstructed slightly each time it is recalled, and details can change in the process. In fact, when experiment participants were repeatedly given suggestions about an event that never happened, some came to firmly believe over time that it actually occurred. This phenomenon is deeply related to the reliability problem of eyewitness testimony. Even a confident eyewitness's testimony, researchers say, cannot rule out the possibility of distortion over time. Researchers point out that memories with strong emotional involvement are actually at greater risk of distortion. This is because intense emotion tends to leave behind an overall impression rather than precise details. These research findings are having a practical impact on how testimony is treated in tribunals.

questions_es.question_es: ¿qué hizo experiment involving false suggestions reveal about memory?
options: Participants came to believe events that never happened
Memory cannot be influenced by suggestion

questions_es.question_es: According to remarrchers, what type of memory is at greater risk of distortion?

b2-explainer_9.body_es: There are cases where someuno who once worked passionately suddenly falls into a state of extreme fatigue and helplessness, unable to do anything. This is called burnout, and the World Health Organization has defined it as a syndrome resulting from chronic workplace stress. People experiencing burnout often blame themselves for not being able to work harder, but experts stress this is not a matter of ability but the result of stress accumulated over a long period. Recovery requires, first, restoring the body's and mind's energy through sufficient rest. But simply resting is not enough, some note, and a process of examining the root cause that led to exhaustion is also needed. Some experts analyze that a habit of shouldering too much responsibility alone, or a perfectionist tendency, is a major cause of burnout. Not feeling ashamed to ask those around you for help during recovery is also cited as important. Ultimately, the path out of burnout lies not in returning completely to how things were before, but in finding a new balance between work and life.

questions_es.question_es: ¿cómo World Health Organization define burnout?
options: A syndrome from chronic workplace stress
A physical illness unrelated to work

questions_es.question_es: What do some experts identify as a major cause of burnout?
options: Shouldering too much responsibility aluno or perfectionism

b2-explainer_10.body_es: Gossip is ofdiez seen as a negative, unproductive behavior, but evolutionary psychologists explain it has served a function of its own in human society. As group size grew in early human societies, making it hard to directly observe every member's behavior, gossip developed as a means of sharing information. Sharing information about who could and could not be trusted provided real benefit to group survival. Research indeed shows that a considerable portion of conversation is filled with talk about other people, a phenomenon common across eras and cultures. Of course, gossip that drifts into baseless slander causes side effects such as damaging relationships and eroding trust. Psychologists advise not viewing gossip itself as unconditionally bad but examining whether it is based on fact and what purpose it serves. In the end, what matters is not whether gossip exists but exercising restraint so it does not drift in a direction that damages relationships.

questions_es.question_es: What function did gossip serve in early human societies, according to evolutionary psychologists?
options: It served as a means of sharing information about trusdosrthiness
It had no function at all
It replaced all other forms of communication

questions_es.question_es: What do psychologists advise about evaluating gossip?
options: Always view it as unconditionally bad
Examine whether it is fact-based and its purpose

b2-explainer_11.title_es: Why do we keep repeating regret?
b2-explainer_11.body_es: Dwelling on and regretting past choices is a common human psychological habit. Interestingly, psychological research shows that people tend to regret things they did not do longer and more intensely than things they did. This is because attempts that failed tend to be accepted over time as learning experiences, whereas things never even attempted keep lingering in the mind. This is called the difference between action regret and inaction regret. Regret tends to be especially long-lasting for moments at major turning points in life when someone gave up on a challenge. Experts say understanding this psychology can offer useful guidance for future decisions. If fear of failure is causing someone to avoid even attempting something, that choice is likely to return as even greater regret later. Ultimately, advice follows that the best way to rojouce regret lies not in guaranteeing a perfect outcome but in having the courage to simply try.

questions_es.question_es: According to the research mentiunod, which type of regret tends to last longer?
options: Regret over things duno and failed

questions_es.question_es: What advice follows from understanding this psychology, de acuerdo al pasaje?
options: Have the courage to simply try

b2-explainer_12.title_es: Do reusable cups really help the environment?
b2-explainer_12.body_es: The number of people using reusable cups instead of disposable ones has noticeably grown. But recent studies point out that this practice is not as simple as it seems. Producing a reusable cup also consumes considerable resources and energy, so discarding it after only a few uses can actually place a greater burden on the environment than a disposable cup. Researchers found that a single reusable cup must be used dozens of times or more to offset the disposable cups it replaces. The problem is that as trendy reusable cup designs are consumed like fashion items, many end up rarely used for long. Experts stress that using what one already owns for as long as possible matters more than buying a new reusable cup. Ultimately, the core of eco-friendly consumption lies not in what you buy but in ¿cuánto tiempo you use it.

questions_es.question_es: What did remarrchers find about the environmental benefit of reusable cups?
options: They should be replaced every week
They must be used dozens of times or more to offset disposables
They have no environmental cost at all
They are always better after just uno use

questions_es.question_es: What do experts say matters most for eco-friendly consumption?
options: Using what you already own for as long as possible

b2-explainer_13.body_es: It is common to see products with a green leaf image and the label \"eco-friendly\" on their packaging. But a growing number of critics point out that such labels do not guarantee actual environmental benefit. This phenomenon, called greenwashing, refers to a mercadoing strategy in which companies try to attract eco-conscious consumers through image alone, without substantive effort. A common example is promoting an entire product as eco-friendly after changing only a tiny portion of its packaging to recycled material. As consumers grow accustomed to such labels, a paradox emerges in which it becomes even harder to identify genuinely eco-friendly products. In response, some countries are drafting legislation to tighten standards for using eco-friendly claims. Experts advise that consumers themselves should form the habit of carefully checking certification marks and ingredient lists. Ultimately, the power to stop greenwashing comes from both regulation and consumers' critical perspective.

b2-explainer_14.title_es: Is a plastic-free day even possible?
b2-explainer_14.body_es: Some people have tried the experiment of going an entire day, from waking up to falling asleep, without touching plastic at all. The result was that it was far harder than expected. Plastic is woven into everyday life, from toothbrushes to shampoo bottles to food packaging. This experiment serves as a fresh reminder of just how deeply plastic is embedded in our lives. If eliminating plastic entirely is realistically impossible, ¿qué es the alternative? Experts suggest aiming not for a perfect zero but for gradually replacing what can be replaced, one item at a time. For example, swapping a plastic toothbrush for a bamboo one, or a plastic bag for a reusable tote. Their explanation is that small practices, added together, can drive change not only in personal consumption habits but also in how companies produce goods.

Plastic is easy to avoid entirely
Plastic is deeply embedded in everyday life

b2-explainer_15.body_es: Fast fashion, which quickly delivers trendy clothes at low prices, has been hugely popular with consumers. But behind it lies a production method that places a heavy burden on the environment. Making a single garment consumes significant agua and energy, and as trends change rapidly, the volume of discarded clothing is surging. Clothes made of synthetic fiber, in particular, release microplastics with every wash, contributing to ocean pollution. As this problem has become known, a culture of wearing clothes longer and mending them for reuse is slowly spreading. Some brands run programs collecting old clothes for recycling to improve their image, but critics say the actual impact is limited. Experts say the fundamental solution is for consumers to slow the pace at which they buy clothes. Rather than chasing trends, it is time to choose clothes carefully with long-term wear in mind.

questions_es.question_es: What environmental problem is linked to synthetic fiber clothing in the passage?
options: It uses no agua to produce

b2-explainer_16.title_es: Why urban beekeeping is on the rise
b2-explainer_16.body_es: Finding beehives on city rooftops or in parques has become a familiar sight. Urban beekeeping, as this activity is called, carries meaning beyond simply harvesting honey — it is tied to ecosystem protection. Bee populations are declining sharply worldwide, a serious problem that could severely disrupt crop pollination. Interestingly, some studies show that cities, with less pesticide use and diverse flowering plants, can actually be safer habitats for bees. In response, several municipalities and companies have begun supporting projects to install beehives on rooftops. However, as urban beekeeping increases, conflicts with neighbors and safety concerns have also been raised. Experts say maintaining proper distance and providing education can sufficiently address such concerns. Urban beekeeping is drawing attention as a new way for people and nature to coexist.

options: Cities are colder than rural areas
Cities have no flowers at all
Cities have less pesticide use and diverse flowers

questions_es.question_es: What concerns have arisen alongside the rise of urban beekeeping?
options: Conflicts with neighbors and safety concerns

b2-explainer_17.body_es: As sudden downpours increasingly flood roads, interest in how cities manage rainwater is growing. With traditional drainage systems struggling to handle heavier rainfall, the so-called sponge city concept has drawn attention as an alternative. It is a design approach that creates plant- and soil-filled spaces between roads and buildings, letting rainwater naturally seep into the ground. Rain jardíns and permeable pavement work on the same principle. This approach not only reduces flood risk but also allows collected rainwater to be stored and reused during droughts. Several cities have adopted this concept in redesigning parks and roads. However, practical difficulties remain, since transforming existing urban structures requires enormous budgets and time. Experts advise that a phased, long-term approach is the realistic solution.

questions_es.question_es: ¿qué es the sponge city concept designed to do?
options: Speed up drainage into ríos only
Let rainagua naturally seep into the ground

questions_es.question_es: What difficulty do experts note about adopting the sponge ciudad concept?
options: It works only in small pueblos
It has already been fully adopted everywhere
It requires enormous budgets and time

b2-explainer_18.body_es: It is increasingly common to find labels displaying a product's carbon emissions as a number on supermercado shelves. Such carbon labels are meant to inform consumers of the amount of greenhouse gas generated throughout a product's production and distribution. The intent behind introducing them is to help consumers make more eco-friendly choices based on information. Indeed, surveys show that sales of relatively lower-carbon products rose after such labels were introduced. However, practical difficulties exist, since accurately measuring and comparing carbon emissions across all products is not easy. Because emissions vary greatly depending on the origin of raw materials or processing methods, unifying standards is itself a complex task. Some companies are also criticized for exploiting this complexity to calculate emissions in ways that favor themselves. Experts point out that establishing trustworthy international standards is a prerequisite for the carbon labeling system to take root.

questions_es.question_es: What is the purpose of carbon labels, de acuerdo al pasaje?
options: To help consumers make more eco-friendly choices
