c1-article_19.title_es: Webtoons go global — and the story behind it
c1-article_19.body_es: Webtoons that originated in Korea are spreading overseas through platforms in various countries, establishing themselves as a new export industry. According to industry data, the share of overseas revenue for domestic webtoon platforms has grown to nearly half in recent years. In particular, as more webtoon originals are adapted into dramas and films, webtoons are also gaining value as a source of intellectual property across the broader condiezt industry. Behind this industry growth, however, debate persists over the treatment of creators. Rookie writers report struggling to make a living due to deadline pressure and low initial manuscript fees. Some writers have been reported to suffer health problems from excessive workload and stress, raising concerns about industry practices. Platform companies say they are expanding support programs for rookie writers and minimum revenue guarantee systems. Creator associations, however, point out that such measures remain limited and fall short of genuine improvement in treatment. As overseas expansion grows, demand for translation and localization staff is also rising, and the industry ecosystem itself appears to be diversifying. For the webtoon industry to sustain its growth, a fair revenue-sharing structure between creators and platforms is likely to be the key factor.

c1-article_20.title_es: Local currencies: divided verdicts on their effectiveness
c1-article_20.body_es: Local currency programs, issued by many local gobiernos with the aim of revitalizing regional economies, have recently come under renewed scrutiny over their actual effectiveness. Local currencies operate by restricting use to small merchant stores in the region while offering a certain discount rate or cashback. Some research presents results showing that sales at small self-employed merchants actually increased after local currencies were introduced. Other research counters that local currency use does not shift consumption from large marts to neighborhood shops, but merely replaces spending consumers would have made anyway with a discounted version of the same spending. In other words, they argue, it functions closer to subsidizing existing consumption with government budget rather than generating new consumption. Local governments invest considerable budget in issuing local currencies, and the debate over cost-effectiveness continues. Some local governments have reduced the discount rate or issuance scale of local currency, citing budget burden. Small merchant associations demand expansion, arguing that local currency at least offers some breathing room in competition against large retailers. Economists advise that properly evaluating the effect of local currency requires examining not just short-term sales increases but also long-term changes in consumption habits. Whether local currency policy can be sustained going forward is said to depend on each local government's fiscal conditions and policy priorities.

c1-article_21.title_es: The cuatro-day workweek experiment: results and limits
c1-article_21.body_es: As some companies pilot a cuatro-day workweek, interest in its outcomes is growing. According to results from a large-scale overseas trial, most participating companies decided to keep the system after the trial ended, and employee stress levels and turnover intentions were found to decrease. Domestically as well, cases of adopting a four-day or 4.5-day workweek are increasing, particularly among IT companies and startups. Companies that adopted it explain that despite fewer working days, productivity did not drop significantly because work focus increased. However, it is also pointed out that these results do not apply equally across all industries. In sectors like manufacturing or services, where working hours and output are directly linked, there are concerns that reducing working days could directly reduce output. From the perspective of small and medium-sized enterprises, a counterargument is raised that reducing working days without additional hiring could actually intensify workload. Labor groups stress the premise that a four-day workweek must be implemented without real wage cuts, warning against attempts by some companies to use it as a pretext to adjust wages. Experts assess that the success of the four-day workweek can vary greatly depending on industry characteristics and detailed design.

c1-article_22.title_es: The shadow the low birth rate casts on the housing mercado
c1-article_22.body_es: As the decline in births continues over the long term, analysts project changes in the future supply-demand structure of the housing market. According to Statistics Korea population projections, the working-age population has already turned to a declining trend, one expected to continue for decades. Real estate research institutions assess that population decline could reduce housing demand over the long term, acting as downward price pressure especially in small and mid-sized regional cities. On the other hand, a counterargument is raised that the rise in single-person households and the pace of household fragmentation could offset much of the effect of population decline. Indeed, while the total population has decreased, the number of households itself has continued to rise steadily until recently. Polarization between the greater Seoul area and regional areas is also cited as a variable. Experts point out that the greater Seoul area, where jobs and infrastructure are concentrated, is relatively less affected by population decline, while regional areas are already experiencing worsening housing vacancy problems. Amid this uncertainty, the construction industry is moving to conservatively adjust new supply volumes. The gobierno has said it will prepare a long-term housing policy roadmap responding to demographic change, but no specific direction has yet been presented. The dominant forecast is that the low birth rate's impact on the housing market will show sharply divergent patterns by region.

The rise of single-person casaholds and household fragmentation

c1-article_23.title_es: AI voice cloning and the copyright dispute
c1-article_23.body_es: AI technology that precisely reproduces a specific person's voice is raising new issues across the entertainment industry. This technology is already being used to restore a deceased singer's voice to release new songs, or to use a voice actor's voice to produce various content. Some in the industry view this technology as a new tool that could expand the horizons of creativity. However, workers in voice-related professions such as voice actors and singers express strong concern about the risk of their voice being trained on and used without their consent. Indeed, overseas, actors' and voice actors' unions have taken collective action demanding clear consent procedures and compensation standards for AI voice and likeness cloning. Similar discussions have begun domestically, but no law has yet clearly defined the concept of publiciudad rights for voice. Experts argue that just as there is publicity rights protection for faces, a separate legal safeguard is needed for voices as well. Technology industry players counter, however, that excessively strict regulation could hinder the growth of the related industry. Copyright authorities in various countries are working to refine the scope of copyright recognition for AI-generated works, and regulation of voice cloning technology is being addressed as an extension of this discussion.

c1-article_24.title_es: verde hydrogen: investment rises, commercialization lags
c1-article_24.body_es: Green hydrogen is drawing attention as an alternative energy source for achieving carbon neutrality, and related investment is rapidly increasing. Green hydrogen is produced by using electricity generated from renewable energy to split water, giving it the advantage of emitting no carbon during production. Major domestic and international energy companies have announced plans one after another to build large-scale green hydrogen production facilities. The gobierno is also expanding subsidies and tax support to foster the green hydrogen industry. Industry officials, however, cite the still much higher production cost of green hydrogen compared to fossil-fuel-based hydrogen or natural gas as the biggest obstacle to commercialization. Unless the cost of renewable power generation falls sufficiently, securing price competitiveness for green hydrogen will remain difficult, they say. It is also pointed out as a limitation that infrastructure for storing and transporting the produced hydrogen has not yet been sufficiently built. Some experts propose that the government mandate green hydrogen use in the public sector to help form an initial market. Other experts, however, take a cautious position that the market should be left to itself while waiting for production costs to fall through technological innovation. It appears that considerable time and investment will still be needed before green hydrogen becomes a genuine pillar of the energy transition.

c1-article_25.title_es: Self-employed debt hovers near a danger line
c1-article_25.body_es: As loan balances held by small merchants and self-employed individuals continue to rise, warnings about the associated debt risk are growing louder. According to Bank of Korea data, the delinquency rate on self-employed loans has steadily risen in recent years, now exceeding pre-pandemic levels. Analysts attribute this to self-employed individuals who relied on loans to survive the sharp sales decline during the pandemic, now struggling to repay principal and interest as high interest rates and weak consumption compound the problem. In particular, the high proportion of multiple debtors who have taken loans from several financial institutions raises concern that if defaults spread, the ripple effect could reach the financial system as a whole. The gobierno has responded by expanding debt restructuring programs and low-interest refinancing loans for the self-employed. Some, however, point out that without a fundamental recovery in sales, such support may only amount to postponing the debt rather than resolving it. Indeed, fixed-cost burdens such as delivery platform fees and rising rents continue to squeeze self-employed profitability. Economists warn that in an economic structure where the self-employed make up an unusually large share, as in Korea, this problem could spread beyond individual business crises into a macroeconomic risk. Suggestions have emerged that resolving the self-employed debt problem requires financial support alongside a social safety net for business conversion or post-closure situations.

c1-article_26.title_es: The remarrch funding gap deepens regional universities' struggles
c1-article_26.body_es: The concentration of domestic universidad research and development funding in a select group of top-ranked universities is being reconfirmed by statistics. According to Ministry of Education data, the top dozen or so universities account for a considerable share of total university research funding, and this concentration has not significantly improved in recent years. Well-funded universities attract excellent researchers and expand advanced equipment, continuing a virtuous cycle of securing even more external research funding. Regional universities, by contrast, are often excluded from this flow because the large-scale research projects they can even apply for are limited from the outset. Some professors at regional universities say that even with excellent research ideas, a lack of initial research infrastructure makes it difficult to even draft a competitive proposal. This is pointed to as one cause of a vicious cycle that further concentrates talented researchers at universities in the greater Seoul area. The government runs separate research funding programs to foster regional universities, but it is pointed out that the budget scale is minimal compared to the research funding of top-ranked universities. Some experts propose restructuring the funding distribution method to account for regional balance, but some in academia counter that distribution unrelated to research competitiveness could actually lower overall research standards. The university research funding gap sits at the point where the values of balanced regional development and research competitiveness collide.

c1-article_27.title_es: The resale luxury mercado grows amid authenticity disputes
c1-article_27.body_es: As more consumers buy secondhand luxury items instead of new products, the luxury resale mercado is growing rapidly. According to a market research firm, the global luxury resale market is expanding faster than the market for new luxury goods. Consumers cite the ability to obtain rare items at relatively lower prices, along with the value of sustainable consumption, as the appeal of the resale market. In line with this trend, several startups operate resale-specialized platforms built around authentication services. As the market grows, however, cases of sophisticated counterfeits slipping into the resale distribution network have also increased. Some consumers have reported damage after items that had passed authentication were later found to be counterfeit. Luxury brand headquarters have stated they will not cooperate with platforms lacking their own authentication systems, keeping a certain distance from the resale market. Some brands, instead, have launched their own certified secondhand trading services, entering the market directly. Experts assess that for the resale market to sustain growth, a trustworthy third-party authentication system and cooperation between brands are essential. Whether the luxury resale market can establish itself as a mature industry is said to depend on building this foundation of trust.

c1-article_28.title_es: Automation in banking reshapes the workforce
c1-article_28.body_es: As the banking sector introduces robotic process automation and AI technology into loan screening and document processing, changes are emerging in workforce structure. According to financial industry data, the number of branches and teller staff at major domestic banks has continuously declined over the past decade. Banks explain that automating repetitive tasks increases processing speed and reduces human error. In one bank's case, the time required to review loan documents reportedly shortened significantly after automation was introduced. Labor unions, however, worry that such changes could ultimately lead to large-scale workforce reductions. Concerns are also raised that elderly customers unfamiliar with digital devices are experiencing inconvenience due to the reduction in offline branches. In response, banks are introducing measures such as operating specialized counters for elderly customers or expanding visiting consultation services. Meanwhile, some analysis suggests that instéd of the simple tasks being replaced by automation, workers are being reassigned to higher-value work such as complex asset management consulting or risk analysis. Experts diagnose that banking automation is simultaneously producing conflicting outcomes — improved efficiency and reduced financial accessibility — and advise that policy consideration is needed to balance these two values.

c1-article_29.title_es: The data center boom and the strain on power grids
c1-article_29.body_es: As the spread of AI services drives a global increase in the construction of data centers requiring massive computation, concerns are growing over power supply and demand. According to analysis by energy-related institutions, data center electricity consumption has risen sharply in recent years, with its share of total electricity consumption reaching the high single digits in some countries. In particular, the high-performance servers needed for training and operating AI models consume far more power than ordinary servers. In some regions where data centers are concentrated, new power supply contracts have reportedly been delayed, or transmission grid expansion has failed to keep pace with demand. Power authorities face the challenge of balancing the attraction of new data centers with the stable operation of existing power grids. Some local gobiernos actively pursue data center attraction, hoping for regional economic benefits, while residents in other areas push back against the environmental burden of transmission tower construction needed to expand power infrastructure. Technology companies are trying to optimize power use by expanding renewable energy procurement contracts and improving data center cooling efficiency. Experts warn, however, that since the AI industry's growth rate is outpacing the rate of power infrastructure expansion, fundamental measures are urgently needed.

c1-article_30.title_es: The retirement-age exdiezsion debate splits generations
c1-article_30.body_es: As population aging coincides with the raised starting age for national pension benefits, discussion of extending the statutory retirement age has flared up again. The current statutory retirement age is sixty, but the national pension benefit starting age is later than that, and the resulting income gap after retirement has long been pointed out as a problem. Business circles call for a cautious approach, arguing that extending the retirement age would increase labor cost burdens and reduce companies' capacity to hire young people. Labor groups, however, maintain that extending the retirement age is urgent precisely to resolve the income gap problem. Interestingly, opinions are divided even within the younger generation on this issue. Some young people worry that extending the retirement age will reduce opportunities for new hiring, while others sympathize with the extension, noting that their parents' generation's retirement insecurity could otherwise be passed on to them as a support burden. Looking at overseas cases, some countries have chosen instead to abolish the retirement age while restructuring wage systems around job duties and performance rather than years of service. Domestically, discussion of converting from a seniority-based wage system to a job-based one is proceeding alongside the retirement-age extension debate. The gobierno has said it will seek a compromise through a labor-management-government council, but given the wide gap between stakeholders' positions, reaching agreement is expected to take considerable time.

c1-article_31.title_es: Signs of saturation in the franchise café market
c1-article_31.body_es: As the number of franchise café shops per capita in Korea has risen to one of the world's highest levels, warnings about market saturation are emerging. According to industry statistics, while the number of stores has steadily increased in recent years, average sales per store have trended flat or even declined. In particular, as price competition among low-cost coffee brands intensifies, some franchisees report struggling to secure profitability under a high-volume, low-margin structure. The relatively low initial startup cost and standardized operating manuals are cited as reasons new brands continue entering the market. However, according to Fair Trade Commission data, the closure rate for coffee shop franchises is not lower than that of other food-service categories. Some experts analyze that the phenomenon of excessive concentration of the same brand or competing brand stores in a specific commercial district is a major cause eroding individual store sales. In response, franchise headquarters are strengthening voluntary agreements to maintain a minimum distance from existing stores when opening new locations. From the consumer's perspective, market competition has a positive side, offering diverse choices and frequent discount promotions. However, as a broader recognition spreads across the industry that quantitative growth has reached its limits, moves to seek new growth strategies such as premiumization or overseas expansion are emerging.

c1-article_32.title_es: K-beauty diversifies exports beyond China dependence
c1-article_32.body_es: Domestic cosmetics exports, once heavily dependent on the Chinese market, have shown a pattern of diversifying export destinations in recent years. According to Korea Customs Service statistics, the share of cosmetics exports to China has declined considerably compared to the past, while exports to the United States, Japan, and Southeast Asia have steadily increased. Industry officials explain that the growing competitiveness of domestic Chinese brands, combined with political factors such as China's informal ban on Korean cultural content, has increased the need to reduce dependence on the Chinese market. In the US market in particular, online distribution channels and social media word-of-mouth are analyzed as driving the growth of small independent brands. Indeed, several domestic indie brands have been reported to achieve considerable sales through online platforms alone, without listing in major retailers. Experts point out, however, that market diversification does not automatically guarantee stable growth. Because regulatory standards and consumer preferences differ by region, a strategy tailored to each individual market is needed, they say. Some large companies are working to boost their responsiveness to each market by building local production facilities or acquiring local companies. The industry is watching whether this diversification trend can both reduce the risk of dependence on a single país and boost the overall competitiveness of the K-beauty industry.

c1-article_33.title_es: Whistleblower protection: the gap between design and reality
c1-article_33.body_es: Although a law protecting whistleblowers who report corporate wrongdoing has been in effect for a long time, questions about its actual effectiveness continue to be raised. According to related statistics, the number of public-interest reports has stédily increased, but the proportion of whistleblowers who say they later suffered disadvantages within their organization also remains considerably high. Whistleblower protection groups point out that even though procedures to prevent identity exposure exist, small organizations have a structural limitation in which it is easy to guess who the whistleblower is. Indeed, cases of whistleblowers suffering personnel disadvantages or ostracism after reporting have been reported multiple times in the media. Companies explain that they are improving the system by expanding internal reporting channels and strengthening anonymity. Labor experts, however, assess that institutional supplements alone are unlikely to overcome the closed nature of organizational culture itself. The considerable time it takes for legal protective measures to be implemented after a report is also cited as a factor that discourages people from reporting. Some countries operate systems paying whistleblowers a portion of recovered ill-gotten gains as a reward, reportedly achieving an effect of incentivizing reports. Calls are growing to strengthen compensation systems domestically by referencing such overseas cases, but discussion has yet to progress due to budget and equity concerns.

options: It is too easy to guess who the whistleblower is
Small organizations have no reporting channels at all

c1-article_34.title_es: Real estate project-financing risk: a looming threat to finance?
c1-article_34.body_es: Warnings continue that concerns over defaults in real estate project financing, or PF, could spread into a broader financial-sector risk. According to Financial Supervisory Service data, the delinquency rate on PF loans has risen noticeably in recent years, with the PF exposure of savings banks and securities firms, which have relatively limited capital buffers, cited as a particular concern. Analysts attribute this to a combination of the real estate downturn and rising construction costs, causing multiple development projects to suffer simultaneously from low pre-sale rates and worsening project viability. Some project sites remain stuck at the bridge-loan stage, unable to convert to main financing, with the project delayed for a prolonged period. Financial authorities are guiding restructuring by winding down high-risk project sites while providing funding to sites capable of normalization. The construction industry, however, worries that unclear criteria for distinguishing viable from unviable projects in this selective restructuring process could actually worsen the credit crunch. Experts, comparing the situation to the 2008 financial crisis, assess that the likelihood of PF defaults spreading into a systemic crisis is limited, while still stressing the ongoing need to manage the soundness of related financial institutions. The gobierno has stated it will additionally activate liquidity supply programs if necessary. Analysts say whether the PF default problem spreads into a broader financial system crisis or achieves a manageable soft landing will depend on the pace of real estate market recovery going forward.

questions_es.question_es: Which institutions' PF exposure is cited as a particular concern?
options: Savings banks and securities firms with limited capital buffers

questions_es.question_es: How do experts compare the current situation to the 2008 financial crisis?
options: They say it is far worse than 2008
They assess systemic spread as limited, though institutional soundness still needs monitoring
They say there is no comparison possible
They claim it has already caused a global crash

c1-article_35.title_es: The platformization of care work: convenience versus precarity
c1-article_35.body_es: Platform-based care services, which mediate elder and child care through mobile applications, are spreading rapidly. Users cite the convenience of being able to hire care workers whenever needed, for however long needed, as the advantage of these services. Companies emphasize reliability, explaining that they have procedures in place to verify caregivers' identity and experience. However, a considerable share of the workforce providing care still contracts as independent business operators, often excluding them from basic protections such as industrial accident insurance or paid leave. Labor groups argue that as care platforms grow, improvements in caregiver treatment must accompany that growth. Indeed, one survey found that a considerable proportion of care workers working through platforms reported difficulties with income instability and sudden schedule changes. From the user's perspective, on the other hand, matching through a platform is sometimes seen as far more transparent and safe compared to previous informal referral methods. The gobierno is preparing certification standards to manage care service quality, while also reviewing plans to expand social insurance coverage for care workers. As care demand continues to rise with population aging, it is pointed out that for care platforms to establish themselves as a sustainable service, they must satisfy both user convenience and worker labor stability.

options: Income instability and sudden schedule changes

questions_es.question_es: What dos goals does the passage say care platforms must satisfy to be sustainable?
options: User convenience and worker labor stability
Faster app updates and more investors

c1-article_36.title_es: Digital nomad visas: a new variable for local economies
c1-article_36.body_es: As remote work becomes widespread, more countries and local gobiernos are introducing digital nomad visas that allow foreign remote workers extended stays. Domestically, some regions have begun implementing eased visa requirements and shared-office support policies to attract digital nomads. Local governments expect that long-term foreign residents will boost local lodging, dining, and consumer spending, benefiting the regional economy. Indeed, in some overseas cities with active digital nomad inflows, related consumer spending has reportedly injected considerable vitality into the local economy. On the other hand, however, it is also pointed out that an increase in long-term foreign residents can drive up rents, worsening housing costs for local residents themselves. In some overseas cities, resident backlash against this side effect has led to a scaling back of digital nomad attraction policies. Domestic experts advise that a cautious approach tailored to regional characteristics is needed, drawing on these overseas cases. In particular, they point out, rather than focusing solely on short-term consumption-boosting effects, the long-term impact on the local housing market must also be considered together. The government plans to gradually expand the digital nomad visa system, but region-specific plans for managing side effects have not yet been specified.

options: Rising rents that worsen housing costs for local residents
A shortage of remote work jobs

options: Scaled back digital nomad attraction policies

c1-article_37.title_es: Traditional mercado modernization: uneven results across regions
c1-article_37.body_es: Analysis shows that the traditional market modernization project, pursued by the gobierno and local governments for decades, is producing contrasting results depending on the region. According to Ministry of SMEs and Startups data, the budget invested in facility improvements such as arcade installation and expanded parking has increased every year, but overall traditional market sales have failed to escape a long-term decline as they lose ground to online shopping and large marts. Some markets, however, are cited as success stories, having increased visitor numbers by attracting young merchants and creating distinctive food alleys. Experts point to a common thread among these success cases: beyond simple facility improvement, there were voluntary transformation efforts by merchant associations and content development that leveraged local characteristics. In contrast, markets that focused only on facility investment without a substantive commercial revitalization strategy often failed to see increased visitors even after remodeling. It is also pointed out that a gap is widening among merchants, between those actively entering online sales channels and those sticking to existing methods. Some local governments are working to close this gap by expanding online sales training and support for listing on delivery apps for merchants. The government has said it will shift its policy direction away from uniform facility support toward market-specific tailored support. Whether traditional markets can re-establish themselves as the center of local commerce is said to depend on the effectiveness of such tailored strategies.

options: Voluntary merchant transformation efforts and locally tailorojo content

Moving from uniform facility support to mercado-specific tailored support
Doubling funding for arcade installation only

c1-article_38.title_es: Carbon border adjustment: a new burden for exporters
c1-article_38.body_es: As the European Union phases in the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism, known as CBAM, domestic exporters in related industries face a new challenge to address. The system is designed to impose costs proportional to carbon emissions generated during production when exporting carbon-intensive items such as steel, cement, and aluminum to the EU. According to an analysis by the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy, a considerable number of domestic exporters in related industries have not yet sufficiently established systems to precisely calculate and report their carbon emissions. Large companies are building their own carbon emission measurement systems, but small and medium-sized supplier firms are slower to respond due to workforce and cost burdens. Industry officials worry that once the system is fully implemented, companies with carbon-intensive production processes could become less price-competitive. Some experts, however, assess that this system could actually accelerate domestic companies' transition to low-carbon production technology. The gobierno has said it will support related industries with funding for low-carbon equipment conversion and expand carbon emission calculation consulting. Small and medium-sized business circles, however, point out that the scale of support remains insufficient compared to the actual conversion costs. As the possibility of the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism spreading to other countries is also being discussed, analysis continues on the impact it could have on the broader Korean economy, given its export-oriented industrial structure.

options: It could accelerate the transition to low-carbon production technology

c1-article_39.title_es: AI digital textbooks arrive — is the classroom ready?
c1-article_39.body_es: As AI digital textbooks, which analyze learning data to provide personalized content for each student, are piloted in some subjects, notable changes are anticipated in classrooms. Education authorities explain that digital textbooks can help reduce learning gaps by adjusting problem difficulty to match each student's pace and comprehension. Indeed, some escuelas participating in the pilot have released internal assessments showing increased student engagement. Among teachers, however, concerns are emerging that the rollout was rushed without sufficient preparation time. Teachers who have not had enough time to master lesson design using digital devices report difficulty planning their classes. Parent groups, worried about the effect of prolonged screen exposure on students' eyesight and concentration, are calling for a cautious approach. Some education experts, on the other hand, argue that since digital transformation is an inevitable trend, continuous improvement should proceed even while accepting initial trial and error. It is also pointed out that regional gaps in digital infrastructure place schools in areas with poor network connectivity at a relative disadvantage. The Ministry of Education has said it will expand teacher training programs and gradually increase the number of subjects covered, but some trial and error appears inevitable before the system becomes firmly established.

options: They are too expensive to distribute
Prolonged screen exposure could affect esíight and concentration

c1-editorial_0.title_es: Time to lower the voting age further
c1-editorial_0.body_es: Discussion about lowering the voting age from 18 to 16 has recently gained momentum again. The core argument is that since teenagers are not entirely free from the duties of military service, taxation, and labor, they should also have a voice in political decisions. Given that many teenagers already work part-time jobs and pay taxes outside of escuela, it is worth reexamining the balance between rights and duties. Of course, some argue that minors have not yet developed independent political judgment and are easily swept up in classroom opinion. This is a point that cannot be dismissed lightly. However, the logic of restricting suffrage itself on the grounds of immature judgment is losing persuasive force in many countries already. Granting suffrage earlier could instead become an opportunity to raise the need for political education and cultivate civic awareness sooner. In conclusion, our society should reexamine the age floor while simultaneously implementing political education in schools to help this system take root.

questions_es.question_es: What position does the editorial take on lowering the voting age?
options: It should not change under any circumstances
It should be lowerojo further, alongside political education
It should be decided by each escuela

options: That teenagers already have too much political power
That minors lack independent political judgment and are easily swayed
That the current age is already too low

c1-editorial_1.title_es: Is the CSAT-centerojo evaluation system still acceptable?
c1-editorial_1.body_es: The current college entrance exam (CSAT) system, which evaluates twelve years of a student's effort through a single day's test, must now be fundamentally reexamined. The CSAT appears to be an objective standard on the surface, but in reality its structure is heavily swayed by how much private tutoring a student has received. The reality that a decade of effort can be overturned by one's condition on test day is far from the original purpose of education. Of course, a formidable counter-view holds that the CSAT is the most objective and transparent system precisely because it evaluates every student with identical questions regardless of school, region, or background. The concern that expanding qualitative evaluation could increase arbitrariness and disputes over fairness also has merit. Nevertheless, the current structure, which places excessive weight on a single test result, is hard to defend against the criticism that it confines students' diverse potential within a uniform standard. In conclusion, the gobierno should gradually reduce the weight of the CSAT and reform the admissions system to include process-based evaluation in parallel.

The CSAT's wocho should be gradually reduced alongside process-based evaluation
The CSAT is already the fairest system possible

options: That the CSAT favors wealthy students only

c1-editorial_2.title_es: Gender pay gap disclosure should be mandatory
c1-editorial_2.body_es: Calls are growing for legislation requiring companies to regularly disclose their gender pay gap. When a gap that has existed only as a statistic becomes visible at the level of individual companies, the substance of the problem becomes concrete and pressure toward genuine improvement begins to function. Mandatory disclosure is less a punishment than a measure to resolve information asymmetry. Both job seekers and investors have a right to know the wage structure, and this also strengthens the market's own self-regulating function. Of course, the business community counters that comparing simple averages while ignoring differences in job role and career length could create misunderstanding and stigma. There is also concern that the added administrative burden could become excessive regulation, especially for small and medium enterprises. These are valid points, but refining the statistics is a problem that can be addressed through system design, not a reason to postpone disclosure itself. In conclusion, the gobierno should move toward mandating gender pay gap disclosure, even if it grants a phased grace period by company size.

questions_es.question_es: What position does the editorial take?
options: Pay gap disclosure should never be requirojo
Disclosure should be mandated, possibly with a phased grace period
Only gobierno agencies should disclose pay data
Wage structures should remain entirely private

questions_es.question_es: What counter-view does the business community raise, de acuerdo al pasaje?
options: That simple average comparisons ignoring job differences could cause misunderstanding and added burden
That disclosure should apply only to large corporations
That employees do not want transparency

c1-editorial_3.title_es: Low birthrate: a crisis requiring state action
c1-editorial_3.body_es: Even though the total fertility rate has long fallen to the lowest level in the world, some still dismiss low birthrates as merely a matter of personal choice. But if structural barriers such as housing costs, private education expenses, and career interruption are distorting that choice itself, this can no longer be left solely to the private sphere. If population decline continues at this pace, the labor force, pension system, and local communities as a whole will be shaken, making this a crisis directly tied to the nation's survival. Of course, there is a counter-view that marriage and childbirth are deeply personal choices, and that it is inappropriate for the state to intervene in the private sphere by leading with cash incentives. The criticism that past pro-natal policies achieved little is also worth heeding. But this only shows that the direction of policy was wrong, not a reason to abandon intervention altogether. In conclusion, the gobierno should urgently pursue a comprehensive approach that addresses the structural problems of housing, childcare, and working hours, beyond cash support alone.

questions_es.question_es: ¿qué es the editorial's stance on low birthrate?
options: It is purely a personal choice with no policy role
It is a structural crisis requiring comprehensive state intervention
efectivo incentives alone have already solved the problem

options: That marriage and childbirth are personal choices the state should not intervene in

c1-editorial_4.body_es: More and more companies are using AI algorithms to screen resumes and evaluate interviews. Their efficiency and cost savings are clear, but underlying this is a fundamental problem: no one can clearly explain by what criteria the algorithm filters applicants. If the training data already contains bias, there is a risk that outcomes unfavorable to a particular gender, age group, or school of origin will be repeatedly reproduced. Given this reality, there is a need to require at least minimal disclosure of the criteria hiring algorithms use. Of course, companies counter that the detailed logic of an algorithm constitutes a trade secret, and that disclosing it could allow the hiring system itself to be gamed. This is a practical concern that cannot be ignored. However, a system in which an external body regularly audits for discriminatory outcomes, rather than requiring full disclosure, could protect trade secrets and secure fairness at the same time. In conclusion, the gobierno should introduce a regular auditing system for algorithmic hiring.

questions_es.question_es: What solution does the editorial propose to balance the dos concerns?
options: Full barlic disclosure of all algorithm code
Regular external audits for discriminatory outcomes without full disclosure
Leaving the matter entirely to companies

questions_es.question_es: What counter-view does the editorial concede?
options: That disclosure could expose trade secrets and invite gaming of the system
That AI hiring should be mandatory everywhere

c1-editorial_5.title_es: Media literacy should become a formal escuela subject
c1-editorial_5.body_es: In an age when fake news and manipulated images spread rapidly through algorithms, the ability to critically read information is no longer optional culture but a basic literacy for survival. Yet in the escuela curriculum, media literacy still holds only a secondary status, roughly equivalent to a creative extracurricular activity. If systematic training in verifying sources and suspecting the possibility of manipulation does not begin in childhood, students will remain vulnerable to misinformation even as adults. Of course, there is a counter-view that adding a new formal subject to an already crowded curriculum is a heavy practical burden. There is also merit to the argument that covering the material within existing subjects like Korean language and social studies is sufficient. However, content handled only in fragments is unlikely to lead to systematic training in thinking. In conclusion, education authorities should institutionalize media literacy education with clear grade-level achievement standards, whether by integrating it into existing subjects or creating an independent one.

options: Removing media literacy from all curricula
Institutionalizing media literacy education with clear standards
Leaving media literacy entirely to parents

options: That media literacy is unnecessary for students
That adding a new formal subject would overburden an already crowded curriculum
That fake news is not a real problem

c1-editorial_6.title_es: The right to disconnect should be legally guaranteed
c1-editorial_6.body_es: The practice of continuing to give work instructions via messenger even after oficina hours is effectively dismantling the boundary of working time. The so-called right to disconnect refers to a discussion about legally guaranteeing workers' freedom not to respond to work contact outside working hours; several countries, including France, already have related regulations. Research is accumulating showing that a culture where being constantly on standby is taken for granted not only erodes workers' mental health in the long run but also negatively affects productivity. Of course, there is a formidable counter-view that in occupations that must respond immediately to emergencies, such a right is unrealistic. Managers also worry that operational flexibility could be excessively constrained. These are valid points, but flexible legislation that allows industry-specific exceptions rather than a blanket ban could resolve much of this concern. In conclusion, our society should legislate the right to disconnect, even if only in stages, in order to protect workers' recovery time.

Phased legislation for the right to disconnect with industry exceptions
Leaving the issue entirely to individual companies

options: That some occupations requiring emergency response make the right unrealistic
That the right to disconnect already exists everywhere

c1-editorial_7.title_es: Is gentrification an unavoidable cost of urban renewal?
c1-editorial_7.body_es: As rundown alleys regain vitality and commercial districts revive, a recurring pattern emerges: rents skyrocket and long-time residents and shop owners are pushed out. Some argue this is simply a natural market outcome of rising local value, and that artificial intervention would only discourage local investment. Looking only at rising property values and tax revenue, this argument may seem plausible at first glance. But considering that it was precisely these long-time residents and merchants who created the area's identity, renewal that excludes them amounts to hollowing the area out. Given this reality, urban renewal should not be left entirely to market logic. Minimal safeguards, such as strengthening commercial lease renewal rights or establishing local co-prosperity funds, should accompany it. In conclusion, local gobiernos should design institutional mechanisms guaranteeing the resettlement of original residents and merchants from the earliest stages of any renewal project.

It should not be left entirely to mercado logic; safeguards for original residents are needed
It should be banned entirely by law

options: That rising rents are a natural mercado outcome and intervention could discourage investment
That old residents always benefit most
That taxes should be lowered instéd

c1-editorial_8.title_es: Platforms must also bear responsibility for spreading misinformation
c1-editorial_8.body_es: Whenever misinformation causes social confusion, platform companies have avoided responsibility by claiming to be mere conduits. But it is hard to view platforms as simply neutral intermediaries, given that the very structure by which algorithms prioritize sensational content to increase user dwell time actively fuels the spread of misinformation. Even when content is user-generated, how it is arranged and amplified depends entirely on the platform's design. Of course, there is a counter-view that requiring pre-screening of every post would chill freedom of expression and is nearly impossible in practice. The concern that imposing excessive responsibility on platforms could also block the normal circulation of information is valid. Nevertheless, imposing an obligation for after-the-fact removal along with minimal transparency requirements on algorithm design could be a compromise that improves the structure of dissemination without infringing on free expression. In conclusion, the gobierno should establish a legal basis requiring platforms to bear after-the-fact response duties and transparency disclosure obligations.

options: After-the-fact removal duties plus algorithm transparency requirements

questions_es.question_es: What counter-view is conceded regarding pre-screening?

That it would chill free expression and is nearly impossible in practice
That platforms already do this voluntarily

c1-editorial_9.body_es: Many companies still treat TOEIC scores or English interviews as a core hiring criterion. But now that translation AI accuracy has improved dramatically, the practice of demanding a uniform English standard even for positions where most work happens domestically deserves reconsideration. Studies consistently show a low correlation between job competence and English test scores. An excessive English standard can even backfire by filtering out talented candidates who possess the actual expertise the job requires. Of course, a counter-view cannot be ignored: for roles involving frequent communication with overseas clients, or at global companies, English ability remains an important practical competence. The claim that language ability itself signals international sensibility and learning capaciudad is also not entirely wrong. But this necessity should be applied differentially by job role, not uniformly demanded across the board. In conclusion, companies should redesign their English requirements by job role, based on actual job relevance.

English requirements should be rojoesigned by job role based on actual relevance

options: That English ability remains important for roles involving frequent overmars communication

c1-editorial_10.title_es: Rural depopulation: infrastructure before efectivo incentives
c1-editorial_10.body_es: Policies in which the gobierno pays settlement incentives to regions at risk of depopulation are spreading, but simply handing out cash to areas lacking hospitals, public transit, and cultural facilities is unlikely to stop the fundamental outflow of population. Young people leave rural areas not because one-time subsidies are insufficient, but because the very foundation for living there long-term is weak. It is hard to persuade someone to raise a child or spend their retirement in a region where the nearest emergency medical facility is an hour away, using cash support alone. Of course, there is a counter-view that immediate financial support shows short-term effects on population inflow, and the practical difficulty that infrastructure investment takes far more time and money cannot be ignored. But experience across many local governments has already confirmed that support limited to short-term effects does not lead to sustainable settlement. In conclusion, the government should prioritize expanding medical, transportation, and childcare infrastructure, even while continuing cash incentives in parallel.

questions_es.question_es: What does the editorial argue should be the policy priority?
options: Expanding medical, transportation, and childcare infrastructure

questions_es.question_es: What counter-view does the passage concede?

c1-editorial_11.title_es: Military service system: fairness must be reexamined
c1-editorial_11.body_es: Controversy over mandatory military service usually flares up only when suspicions of draft evasion by certain groups surface, then quickly fades. But the essence of the problem lies not in individual cases but in the system itself. Even with identical physical conditions, there is room for arbitrary application of grading criteria, and a compensation system for the economic losses incurred during service is effectively absent. Given this reality, it is time to reexamine the fairness of the military service system. Of course, there is a counter-view that, given its special purpose of national security, ordinary equity logic cannot be simply applied to this system. There is also concern that overly granular grading criteria could increase the potential for abuse. But the special nature of national security cannot justify opacity in the grading process. In conclusion, the gobierno should raise the transparency of the grading process and establish a genuine compensation system for service in order to restore trust in the military service system.

questions_es.question_es: What does the editorial identify as the essence of the problem?
options: The system itself, including arbitrary grading and lack of compensation
The length of service being too short

questions_es.question_es: What counter-view is conceded in the passage?
options: That ordinary equity logic is hard to apply given the security purpose of the system
That the system needs no reform at all
That grading criteria are already fully transparent

c1-editorial_12.body_es: Cases keep repeating in which people who exposed wrongdoing inside their organizations suffer dismissal, lawsuits, and cold treatment from colleagues instéd of protection. Despite the existence of a whistleblower protection law, criticism that it lacks real effectiveness persists because the burden of proving retaliatory action falls excessively on the whistleblower. In a structure where organizational power and individual power are inherently unequal from the start, this imbalance in the burden of proof ultimately discourages whistleblowing itself. Of course, organizations counter that an increase in baseless, reckless exposure could damage internal trust and work efficiency. It is also true that there have been cases of false reports stemming from personal grievance. But this is a problem to be resolved through a separate verification process for the truth of the report, not grounds for lowering the level of whistleblower protection. In conclusion, the National Assembly should revise the relevant law to shift some of the burden of proof onto organizations and strengthen penalties for retaliatory action.

questions_es.question_es: What structural problem does the editorial identify?
options: Whistleblowers have too much legal power already
The burden of proving retaliation falls excessively on the whistleblower
There are no whistleblower laws at all
Organizations are too weak to retaliate

questions_es.question_es: What counter-view does the editorial concede?
options: That reckless or false reports could damage internal trust and efficiency
That current protections are already too strong

c1-editorial_13.title_es: The 'ppalli-ppalli' culture is no longer a competitive edge
c1-editorial_13.body_es: The so-called ppalli-ppalli, or 'hurry hurry,' culture that prioritizes speed above all else was once praised as the driving force behind compressed economic growth. Today, however, there is growing criticism that this culture causes safety checks to be skipped and pushes decisions through without sufficient discussion. When the race for speed goes too far, it erodes even the time that should go into quality control and long-term strategy. Indeed, behind many industrial accidents and shoddy construction cases lay a practice that treated shortening the schedule as the top priority. Of course, there is a counter-view that swift decision-making and execution remain an important competitive factor in fast-changing markets. Indeed, there are no shortage of cases where companies overcame a crisis thanks to rapid response. But speed and prudence are not incompatible values. In conclusion, companies and the gobierno should establish institutional standards so that minimum safety and verification procedures are never skipped in the name of speed.

options: It makes the economy grow too slowly
It leads to skipped safety cuentas and rushed decisions
It has no relationship to industrial accidents
It is only a problem in small companies

questions_es.question_es: What counter-view does the editorial acknowledge?
options: That speed is now completely worthless
That swift decision-making remains a valuable competitive factor in fast-changing mercados
That all companies have abandunod speed already

c1-editorial_14.title_es: barlic data should be opened more boldly
c1-editorial_14.body_es: The vast troves of data held by the gobierno and public institutions are already a public good created with taxpayer money, yet a considerable portion still lies dormant, undisclosed. Cases both at home and abroad have already sufficiently demonstrated that when transportation, medical, and climate data are opened up, the private sector uses them to create new services and industries. Hoarding data actually undermines the public interest. Of course, the counter-view that opening data containing personal information increases the risk of leaks and misuse is by no means a minor concern. The point that anonymization is never perfect, leaving a residual risk of re-identification, is also valid. But this is not a reason to abandon full disclosure — rather, it is a reason to refine anonymization technology and access-management systems. In conclusion, the government should expand the scope and pace of public data disclosure more boldly, on the premise of advancing personal-information protection technology.

barlic data should be opened more boldly, alongside better anonymization technology

All personal data should be permanently deleted

That public data has no value to anyuno

c1-editorial_15.title_es: Carbon neutrality is impossible without nuclear power
c1-editorial_15.body_es: Attempting to move toward carbon neutrality while excluding nuclear power inevitably runs into practical limits. It is true that the cost of renewable energy generation is falling, but large-scale storage technology to overcome its intermittency has not yet reached commercial viability. Given this reality, there is a need to make transitional use of nuclear power, which supplies stable baseline electricity without carbon emissions. Of course, there are considerable voices opposing the expansion of nuclear power because of radioactive waste disposal and the risk of accidents. The vigilance left behind by the Fukushima accident is a legacy that cannot be taken lightly. But the safety standards of modern nuclear plants have been strengthened beyond comparison with the past, and waste treatment technology continues to advance steadily. If the goal of achieving carbon neutrality with renewables alone is unrealistic, then conducting the discussion while excluding nuclear power altogether is itself irresponsible. In conclusion, the gobierno should include nuclear power as one pillar of its carbon neutrality strategy, on the condition that safety standards remain the top priority.

options: It should be banned entirely due to safety risks
It should be included as uno pillar of carbon neutrality strategy, with safety as top priority
Only renewables should ever be used
Nuclear power has no relation to carbon neutrality

questions_es.question_es: What counter-view does the editorial formally acknowledge?
options: That renewables are already sufficient for carbon neutrality

c1-editorial_16.title_es: Influencer undisclosed ads need stronger regulation
c1-editorial_16.body_es: The so-called undisclosed advertising practice — receiving sponsorship without disclosing it and presenting content as a genuine recommendation — has still not been eradicated. Current labeling and advertising law regulates this behavior, but questions about its real effectiveness persist, since penalties are light and violators often simply switch accounts and continue after being caught. Consumers make purchasing decisions they would not have made had they known it was an advertisement, mistaking it for a genuine recommendation — a clear act of deception. Of course, the creator industry counters that excessive regulation could chill freedom of expression and new forms of creative activity. There is also a point that overly rigid disclosure formats could undermine the natural feel of content. But this counter-view is weak, since strengthening disclosure requirements does not block creation itself but merely demands minimal transparency. In conclusion, the gobierno should substantially raise penalty levels and mandate the introduction of automatic detection systems at the platform level.

questions_es.question_es: What does the editorial ultimately recommend?
options: Raising penalties and mandating automatic detection systems on platforms

It finds the counter-view weak since disclosure only requires minimal transparency, not a ban on creation
It argues creators should be banned from advertising

c1-editorial_17.title_es: Unpaid overtime must now be enforced against
c1-editorial_17.body_es: It is not an unusual sight for office lights to stay on well after regular working hours end. The problem is that much of this extended work goes unreported and is carried out as an unpaid, customary practice. Even though the Labor Standards Act explicitly requires overtime pay, unpaid overtime is often taken for granted on the ground under implicit pressure. This is not merely an individual worker's problem; it expands into a social problem that distorts working-hour statistics themselves. Of course, there is a valid counter-view that discretionary work exists whose nature is hard to measure strictly by the clock. The point that time-based overtime pay could actually be inefficient for performance-evaluated roles also cannot be ignored. But such exceptions must be premised on clear standards and prior agreement, and should not be left unregulated under the name of custom, as they are now. In conclusion, the gobierno should drastically strengthen mandatory time-recording and on-site labor inspections to genuinely eradicate unpaid overtime.

rojoucing the length of the standard workday

That the Labor Standards Act does not require overtime pay

c1-editorial_18.title_es: Universal basic income is worth piloting
c1-editorial_18.body_es: As predictions gain traction that automation and AI will fundamentally reshape the job structure, discussion of universal basic income — paying every citizen a fixed amount unconditionally — is resurfacing. Since existing selective welfare comes with administrative costs of proving eligibility and a stigmatizing effect, basic income is cited as an alternative that could reduce these side effects. Of course, the counter-view about enormous fiscal burden and reduced work motivation cannot be dismissed lightly. The concern that tax increases needed to fund it could return as another form of burden is also valid. Indeed, some countries' experiments reported noticeably reduced working hours. But such concerns are matters to be empirically verified through pilot programs in limited regions and scale, not full nationwide rollout, and are not reason enough to block the discussion itself. In conclusion, the gobierno should verify both fiscal sustainability and social effects together through a basic income pilot program targeting specific regions or groups.

Replacing all welfare with tax cuts

That automation will not affect jobs

c1-editorial_19.title_es: Real estate speculation can be curbed by policy
c1-editorial_19.body_es: Whenever housing prices surge, skepticism inevitably appears claiming that gobierno regulation only distorts the market and cannot be a fundamental solution. But this skepticism is the result of oversimplifying the market by failing to distinguish speculative demand from genuine housing need. Data confirms that policies such as strengthened taxation on multiple-home owners, loan regulation, and real-residence requirements have, in several past periods, genuinely curbed speculative transactions. Of course, the counter-view that excessive regulation can cause a lock-in effect on listings, shrinking supply and pushing prices even higher, is a point that must be considered in policy design. The point that side effects can grow if regulation to suppress speculative demand is not paired with policy to increase supply is also valid. But this means policy combinations need refinement, not that intervention itself is meaningless. In conclusion, the government should maintain a consistent policy stance that pursues both suppressing speculation and expanding supply at the same time.

c1-editorial_20.title_es: Regional minimum wage differentiation is undesirable
c1-editorial_20.body_es: The business community has consistently raised the argument that the minimum wage should be differentiated by region to reflect differences in cost of living. The logic is that, given lower rents and living costs in rural areas, a single nationwide minimum wage places an excessive burden on small local business owners. But this argument directly conflicts with the original purpose of the minimum wage system: guaranteeing a minimal decent life regardless of where one lives. Lowering the minimum wage by region also carries a real risk of accelerating the already serious outflow of rural population. Of course, the counter-view that a uniform standard ignoring local economic conditions is driving small business owners to close is not a light matter, reflecting real desperation on the ground. It is also true that regional price differences significantly affect real wages. But this problem should be solved through separate fiscal support for small business owners, not by lowering the minimum wage. In conclusion, the gobierno should design policy to maintain the nationwide single minimum wage system while strengthening regional support measures for small business owners.

It is undesirable; a uniform wage should be kept with separate regional support instéd

Only rural areas should have a minimum wage

options: That a uniform standard ignoring local conditions is driving small businesses to close
That rural living costs are higher than urban unos

c1-editorial_21.title_es: Platform workers: close the workers' comp gap
c1-editorial_21.body_es: The number of workers operating through platforms — delivery riders, designated drivers, house cleaners — is rapidly growing, but many of them remain outside the protection of workers' compensation insurance. Classified as special-type workers, they are treated as independent contractors, making it difficult to receive workers' comp even when injured, while platform companies shift responsibility by claiming to be mere intermediaries rather than employers. This gap — where workers are structurally directed and controlled yet legally remain classified as independent contractors — creates the coverage blind spot. Of course, platform companies counter that converting large numbers of workers to direct employment could shake the business model itself. There is also some validity to the claim that flexible work arrangements are what workers themselves actually want. But flexibility and a minimal safety net are compatible values, and one cannot be sacrificed for the other. In conclusion, the gobierno should expand the scope of workers' compensation coverage based on whether genuine direction and supervision exist.

options: That converting workers to direct employment could shake platform business models

c1-editorial_22.title_es: Support for multicultural family children's education should increase
c1-editorial_22.body_es: The number of children from multicultural families keeps rising, but language and learning support for them still varies greatly by region and escuela. Not a few struggle with Korean language learning due to differences in the home language environment, yet a view persists in schools that attributes this to a lack of individual effort. Given that early language gaps lead to broader learning gaps, which risk hardening into gaps after entering society, this is an issue society as a whole must bear, not the individual. Of course, there is a counter-view that expanding support for a specific group could raise fairness concerns with other vulnerable student groups. The point that concentrating limited education budgets on one group is unjust also has some merit. But the language barrier unique to children of multicultural families is a distinct problem that should be addressed separately from general support for vulnerable groups. In conclusion, education authorities should maintain existing support for vulnerable groups while establishing a separate support system to close the language gap.

c1-editorial_23.title_es: Raising the basic pension can no longer be delayed
c1-editorial_23.body_es: Even though the elderly poverty rate remains among the highest in the OECD, discussion of raising the basic pension has repeatedly been pushed back on grounds of fiscal burden. The reality that people who worked their whole lives cannot secure even a minimal livelihood in old age is not individual failure but the result of a social structure that failed to build adequate retirement infrastructure during rapid industrialization. Given this reality, raising the basic pension should be seen not as charitable welfare but as a minimal duty the state ought to fulfill. Of course, the counter-view that expanding pension spending threatens fiscal sustainability, as the supporting population shrinks and the recipient population grows amid low birthrates and aging, is by no means minor. The point about shifting the burden onto future generations should also be taken seriously. But this is not a reason to delay the increase itself — rather, it is a reason to design the funding method together with it. In conclusion, the gobierno should actively address elderly poverty by devising phased increases and funding measures simultaneously.

options: A charitable gesture the state mayo choose to skip
A minimal duty the state ought to fulfill, not charity
An unnecessary expense with no justification
A problem only individuals can solve

options: That elderly poverty does not exist

c1-editorial_24.title_es: Credentialism: must first break down universidad rankings
c1-editorial_24.body_es: Credentialism, in which one's alma mater follows a person like a lifelong label, is an outdated practice that judges a person's potential not by ability but by a test score taken around age twenty. The root of the problem lies not in individual perception but in the rigid ranking structure topped by a handful of universities. In a reality where this ranking affects hiring, promotion, and even the marriage market, telling individuals not to care about their alma mater is nothing more than an empty lecture. Of course, there is a counter-view that ranking among universities is a natural result reflecting some real difference in educational quality, and that artificially eliminating it could actually worsen information asymmetry. The point that ranking functions as an efficient signal for companies needing to distinguish talented candidates also cannot be ignored. But the current way in which ranking oversimplifies individual students' effort and potential to determine lifelong opportunity is clearly excessive. In conclusion, the government and companies should gradually reduce the influence of universidad ranking through expanded blind hiring and more balanced funding among universities.

options: The rigid ranking structure among universities

questions_es.question_es: What counter-view does the editorial concede?
options: That universidad rankings reflect real quality differences and function as an efficient hiring signal

That blind hiring has no benefits

c1-editorial_25.title_es: Time to introduce a pet ownership tax
c1-editorial_25.body_es: As the number of households raising pets rises sharply, the social costs of stray animal protection and related administrative services are rising along with it. But these costs are covered by taxes paid by everyone regardless of pet ownership, raising a persistent fairness concern. Introducing a pet ownership tax and using the proceeds to expand shelters and animal welfare policy would align with the beneficiary-pays principle and could also curb indiscriminate breeding. Of course, a strong counter-view holds that imposing an additional tax on pet owners who already bear considerable costs for food and medical care amounts to double burden. The concern that a tax could actually increase illegal abandonment by owners trying to avoid registration is also valid. But such side effects can be substantially mitigated by designing a reasonable tax rate alongside an improved registration system. In conclusion, the gobierno should consider introducing the ownership tax starting at a low rate, aimed at securing a stable source of funding for animal welfare.

c1-editorial_26.title_es: Youth housing: the barlic sector must step up
c1-editorial_26.body_es: Soaring rental costs are cited as one of the key factors causing young people to repeatedly delay moving out, marriage, and childbirth. Awareness is spreading that the current structure, which leaves the matter entirely to the private rental market, cannot solve this problem. Substantially increasing the supply of public rental housing and expanding low-interest loans for young people should be seen not as mere charity but as investment supporting the next generation's entry into society. Of course, the counter-view that excessive public intervention in the market could reduce private landlords' incentive to supply housing, shrinking overall housing supply in the long run, is a point that must be carefully examined in policy design. The concern that the fiscal burden could grow excessive also cannot be ignored. But if the youth housing problem is left entirely to market logic, there is effectively no other actor to fill the gap, making expanded public involvement unavoidable. In conclusion, the gobierno should expand both public rental housing and financial support simultaneously, without shrinking private supply.

Expanding barlic rental housing and financial support without shrinking private supply

options: That excessive public intervention could rojouce private supply incentives long-term

That barlic housing has no fiscal cost

c1-editorial_27.body_es: Telemedicine has already become a practical alternative in many countries for patients living in areas with poor medical access or for chronically ill patients with limited mobility. In Korea, however, it is still only permitted in a limited way under the name of a pilot program, and full institutionalization keeps being postponed. Given this reality, there is a need to widen the scope of telemedicine's use as a complement to, rather than a replacement for, in-person care. Of course, the medical community strongly counters that misdiagnosis risk grows without an in-person exam, especially for a first visit where accurate diagnosis is difficult. The concern that patients could increasingly concentrate at large hospitals, threatening the survival of neighborhood clinics, is also valid. But this risk can be substantially resolved by limiting telemedicine to follow-up visits and chronic disease management, excluding first visits. In conclusion, the gobierno should institutionalize telemedicine step by step, starting with areas of low misdiagnosis risk, in order to genuinely improve healthcare access.

Replacing all in-person care with telemedicine immediately

options: That misdiagnosis risk grows without in-person exams, especially for first visits
That telemedicine is already fully institutionalized

c1-editorial_28.title_es: ESG management should now be mandatory
c1-editorial_28.body_es: ESG management — environmental, social, and governance factors — has largely been treated as a voluntary promotional tool for companies. But voluntary disclosure has a clear limitation: standards differ from company to company, making it difficult for investors and consumers to compare actual performance. Repeated cases of so-called greenwashing, where some companies dress up promotional language without genuine improvement, also stem from this loophole in voluntary self-regulation. Of course, a formidable counter-view holds that, for small and medium enterprises, the personnel and cost required to build an ESG disclosure system itself becomes a significant barrier to entry. The concern that uniform mandating could actually undermine industrial competitiveness also has merit. But this burden can be sufficiently eased through phased application by company size and gobierno consulting support. In conclusion, the government should mandate ESG disclosure starting with large corporations first, while providing support measures for small and medium enterprises in parallel.

Requiring every company to disclose identically overnoche

options: That ESG disclosure costs create a significant entry barrier for SMEs

c1-editorial_29.title_es: Abolishing the death penalty is the answer
c1-editorial_29.body_es: Korea has effectively become classified as abolitionist in practice, having suspended executions for a long time, yet the system itself still remains on the books. Whenever a brutal crime occurs, barlic opinion demanding the resumption of executions boils over, but clear empirical evidence that the death penalty actually deters violent crime has never been firmly established. Moreover, since there is absolutely no way to reverse the execution of an innocent person wrongly convicted, the death penalty directly conflicts with the inherent imperfection of the judicial system. Of course, the counter-view that perpetrators deserve the ultimate punishment, given the suffering of victims and bereaved families of brutal crimes, cannot be dismissed as mere emotional excess. There is also a point that it is premature to conclude the penalty has zero deterrent effect. But maintaining an irreversible punishment while its deterrent effect remains uncertain is a choice carrying greater risk than justice. In conclusion, the state should formally abolish the death penalty and establish an alternative punishment system, such as life imprisonment without parole.

c1-editorial_30.title_es: Discussion of the number of lawmakers cannot be avoided
c1-editorial_30.body_es: Discussion of the number of National Assembly members flares up briefly during every election season, then disappears. Public antipathy toward the cost of lawmaker salaries is so strong that even politicians hesitate to actively raise the discussion. But looking only at the number of lawmakers relative to population, Korea is by no means high comparojo to other advanced countries; rather, there is persistent criticism that each district represents too large a population, diluting representation. Given this reality, the discussion of the total number should not be narrowed down to only the salary issue. Of course, the counter-view that increasing the number of lawmakers would only increase privileges and budget waste is understandable, reflecting accumulated distrust. It is also true that an increase is realistically hard for public sentiment to accept. But if this issue is discussed together with freezing salaries or reducing privileges, adjusting the number and political reform could be achieved simultaneously. In conclusion, the political establishment should bring the issue of lawmaker numbers into public discourse, premised on reforming the salary structure.

Bring the issue into barlic discourse, tied to salary structure reform
