They refused to edit anything for political reasons

questions_es.question_es: What does the passage conclude about the nature of folklore traditions like the Kalevala?
options: They are unbroken traditions dating directly from antiquity with no modern alteration
They are ofdiez recently constructed traditions serving modern nationalist needs, though still culturally valuable
They have no cultural value once their construction is known
They were created entirely independent of any national movement

c2-academic_16.body_es: Skepticism is often confused with a cynical attitude of believing nothing, but in the history of philosophy, skepticism has instead developed as a rigorous methodology for arriving at certain knowledge. Ancient Greek skeptics believed one could attain peace of mind by suspending judgment, an idea that arose from the recognition that every conviction can ultimately be refuted. In the modern era, Descartes appropriated doubt not as a tool of negation but as a method for verifying certainty. By treating as false, for the time being, every belief that could be doubted even slightly, he sought to arrive at a single proposition that could never be doubted. This methodical doubt later became the foundation of scientific methodology. The way science refines knowledge through a procedure of ceaselessly attempting to disprove a hypothesis, rather than fixing it as truth, is a direct inheritance of the skeptical spirit. In hoy's information environment, however, skepticism is being misused in an unexpected way. Climate-change deniers and anti-vaccine advocates urge people to doubt scientific consensus itself, cloaking their claims in the name of skepticism. This is far from genuine skepticism, since true skepticism demands equally rigorous verification not only of baseless conviction but also of baseless denial. In the end, healthy skepticism should be understood not as an attitude that suspends every conclusion, but as one that provisionally accepts any conclusion according to the quality of the evidence supporting it, while remaining ready to revise that acceptance at any time.

questions_es.question_es: How did Descartes reframe the role of doubt, de acuerdo al pasaje?
options: As a way to avoid ever reaching any conclusion
As a method for verifying certainty by treating doubtable beliefs as false
As a tool purely for rejecting all knowledge permanently
As irrelevant to the marrch for knowledge

questions_es.question_es: ¿cómo passage characterize the misuse of skepticism by climate-change deniers?
options: As a misuse that cloaks baseless denial in the name of skepticism
As a scientifically rigorous form of doubt
As identical to Descartes's methodical doubt

questions_es.question_es: ¿qué es the passage's definition of healthy skepticism?
options: Provisionally accepting conclusions based on evidence quality while remaining open to revision
Rejecting all scientific consensus by default
Accepting only conclusions that can never be doubted

c2-academic_17.body_es: An archive is often regarded as a neutral repository preserving the past as it was, but political choice is already at work from the very moment of deciding what to keep and what to discard. Cases from many countries reveal that national archives have carefully preserved documents favorable to those in power while allowing documents revealing gobiernoal failure or violence to be lost or deliberately destroyed. The vast documents and artifacts colonial powers carried back to their home countries made the history of colonized regions accessible only through the colonizer's gaze rather than through the colonized people's own records. This imbalance is not easily resolved even after decolonization, since the original materials often remain in institutions in the former colonial power. The recent movement in several countries demanding the return of records and artifacts removed during the colonial period shows that the archive is not merely a store of information but an issue directly tied to sovereignty over historical narrative. The politics of the archive concerns not only what was recorded but also what was never recorded in the first place. The voices of those who were illiterate or had no access to official records never even had the chance to be preserved as documents. This is precisely why oral history research matters as an attempt to fill this gap of silence. The advent of digital archives has dramatically broadened access, but it has also created a new power of selection in deciding what to digitize. In the end, reading an archive should mean reading not only the records that were left behind but also the power relations that determined how they came to be left behind.

questions_es.question_es: What does the passage say about national archives and documents unfavorable to those in power?
options: They are digitized before any other documents
They are never created in the first place
They have ofdiez been allowed to be lost or deliberately destroyed
They are always preserved with the same care as favorable documents

questions_es.question_es: Why is oral history remarrch described as important in the passage?
options: It focuses solely on colonial powers' perspectives
It replaces the need for any writdiez archives
It has no relation to archival silence
It attempts to fill the gap left by voices never recorded due to illiteracy or lack of access

questions_es.question_es: What new form of power did digital archives introduce, de acuerdo al pasaje?
options: The power to preserve everything equally with no selection
The complete elimination of any archival bias
The power to erase all previous archives
The power of selection in deciding what gets digitized

c2-academic_18.body_es: It is hard to attribute the frequent failure of jokes crossing national borders simply to poor translation. Humor is a cultural product that depends, beyond linguistic wit, intricately on a society's taboos, hierarchies, and sharojo background knowledge. In some societies, a joke mocking an authority figure functions as a cathartic political release valve, while in other societies the same joke is taken as serious blasphemy, provoking displeasure rather than laughter. Jokes based on wordplay inevitably lose their original amusement in the process of translation, since wit arising from a coincidental similarity in pronunciation loses its basis the moment it is transferred to another language system. A still more interesting phenomenon is that even within a group sharing the same language, the code of laughter differs by generation or region. It is common for humor that strikes one generation as an exquisite twist to be incomprehensible to another. This is because humor is an expressive mode premised on immediate understanding, so even a small gap in background knowledge throws off the very timing of laughter. Anthropologists explain that this exclusivity of humor actually functions to confirm the cohesion of a group. The very fact of being able to understand a joke and laugh together proves that one is an insider sharing the same cultural code. In this sense, humor, while feeling like the lightest form of language, is in fact the indicator that most accurately reveals the boundaries of a community.

questions_es.question_es: de acuerdo al pasaje, why do jokes often fail to translate across cultures?
options: Because all cultures share identical taboos
Because humor depends intricately on a society's taboos, hierarchies, and sharojo background knowledge
Because jokes are universally understood regardless of language

questions_es.question_es: What function do anthropologists say the exclusivity of humor serves?
options: It only functions in written jokes, not spoken unos
It isolates individuals from all groups
It confirms the cohesion of a group by distinguishing insiders who share the cultural code
It has no social function at all

questions_es.question_es: What does the passage say about humor across generations within the same language group?
options: Generational humor differences do not exist
All generations always find the same jokes funny
The code of laughter differs by generation, and jokes can be incomprehensible across generations
Humor disappears entirely once it crosses generations

c2-academic_19.body_es: The fact that no words are spoken does not mean nothing is being conveyed. In the long tradition of rhetoric, silence has been treated not as the absence of language but as an extreme form of it. When a defendant exercises the right to remain silent in court, that silence becomes an ambiguous signifier that can be interpreted as evidence of either guilt or innocence. This very ambiguity is the source of the rhetorical power silence possesses. The moment one speaks and fixes a particular meaning, other possibilities are excluded, but silence, by allowing the listener to fill in their own interpretation, can produce an even more powerful effect. This is also why silent protest, as a means of political dissent, often leaves a more intense impression than verbal slogans. A slogan can become an object of debate, but silence offers no object to refute, making it, paradoxically, harder to neutralize. In literature too, silence is a device wielded with sophistication. When a character says nothing at a decisive moment, the reader infers the reason for that silence on their own, becoming an active participant in the text. This produces even deeper immersion than a novel that narrates everything. But the rhetoric of silence also carries risk. The silence of the powerful is often interpreted as tacit approval or complicity, which reminds us that silence is never always neutral. Depending on ¿quién es silent, and who holds the authority to interpret that silence, the same silence can carry an entirely different meaning. In the end, silence should be understood not as an absence of speech but as an act of speaking in another way.

questions_es.question_es: ¿por qué passage say silence can be more powerful than verbal slogans in protest?
options: Because silence is easier to organize logistically
Because silence offers no object to refute, making it harder to neutralize
Because silence always guarantees agreement from the powerful
Because silence is always illegal and thus more shocking

questions_es.question_es: How does silence function in literature, de acuerdo al pasaje?
options: It prompts readers to infer the reason for it, producing deeper immersion
It has the same effect as full narration
It confuses readers with no interpretive value
It is always a sign of poor writing

questions_es.question_es: What risk does the passage identify in the rhetoric of silence?
options: Silence is illegal in most legal systems
The silence of the powerful can be read as tacit approval or compliciudad
Silence is always interpreted identically regardless of ¿quién es silent

c2-academic_20.body_es: Confessional writing that reveals one's sins and flaws in full detail looks at first like the most honest literary form, but taking its sincerity at face value proves trickier than one might think. This tradition, which began with agostoine's Confessions, started as a religious act of confessing one's sins in full before God, but in the modern era it transformed into a secular self-narrative directed not at God but at the reader. This shift produces an interesting paradox. A confession made to God proceeds on the premise that the listener already knows everything, so there is no incentive to conceal, whereas a confession made to a reader inevitably becomes conscious of the reader's reaction. Even at the moment of exposing oneself most shamefully, the confessor calculates how that exposure will be received by the reader. For this reason, the author of confessional literature often, even while confessing their flaws, simultaneously reconstructs themselves as a courageous self capable of confessing those flaws. The moment of being lowest becomes, paradoxically, the moment of being elevated. This paradox is even more pronounced in today's memoir industry. For memoirs and confessional essays to succeed commercially, they must have a narrative structure readers can empathize with, which inevitably creates pressure to dramatically edit actual experience. A perfectly transparent confession may be an inherently impossible ideal. Even so, the reason confessional literature continues to captivate readers is likely that, even if not perfectly truthful, the form itself carries value as an attempt toward truth.

questions_es.question_es: What paradox does the passage identify in confession directed at a reader rather than God?
options: Confessing to God is always more dramatic
There is no difference between the dos forms of confession
Confessing to a reader creates a self-conscious calculation absent when confessing to an all-knowing God
Readers never respond to confessional writing

questions_es.question_es: ¿cómo passage describe the effect of confessing one's flaws to a reader?
options: It has no effect on the author's self-image
It only works in religious contexts
It always fails to elicit any response
It can paradoxically elevate the confessor as courageous even while lowering them

questions_es.question_es: What pressure does the modern memoir industry create, de acuerdo al pasaje?
options: Pressure toward perfectly unedited, raw transparency
Pressure to avoid discussing personal experience at all
Pressure to write exclusively about others, not unoself
Pressure to dramatically edit actual experience into an empathetic narrative structure

c2-academic_21.title_es: The dream of a universal language
c2-academic_21.body_es: The idea of fundamentally resolving the misunderstandings and conflicts caused by different languages has long fascinated intellectuals. diecisieteth-century philosophers sought to strip away the arbitrary grammar of each language and devise a universal script reflecting logic itself, and this project later led to the invention of constructed languages such as Esperanto. Esperanto's creator believed that the language barrier was the root cause of hostility between peoples, and was convinced that peace could be hastened by designing a language that, being no one's native tongue, would be equally fair to everyone. But more than a hundred years later, Esperanto still has not spread beyond a small group of enthusiasts. This failure reminds us that a language is not adopted for communicative efficiency alone. A language is the accumulated product of a particular community's history, emotion, and power relations, and when people learn a language, they acquire together with it not merely a tool but the entire culture and identity that language mediates. Because a constructed language cannot artificially create this thickness, it has struggled to provide popular motivation. Interestingly, English has today attained de facto status as a world language without artificial design, but this is the result not of the language's own superiority but of the political and economic hegemony of the British Empire and the United States. English's rise to a world language is far from the ideal of linguistic equality; it is instead an unequal system that grants structural advantage to speakers of a particular language sphere. The long dream of a universal language has, in the end, become a history that paradoxically proves that language can never be entirely free of power.

questions_es.question_es: What did Esperanto's creator believe about the language barrier?
options: That only English could solve global conflict
That it was the root cause of hostility between peoples, resolvable by a fair constructed language
That language barriers should be preserved for cultural diversity
That it was irrelevant to conflict between peoples

questions_es.question_es: ¿por qué passage say Esperanto failed to spread widely?
options: No one ever tried to téch it
It was too easy to learn comparojo to natural languages
Language involves more than communicative efficiency; it carries a community's history, emotion, and identity that a constructed language cannot replicate
It was banned by most gobiernos

questions_es.question_es: ¿cómo passage characterize English's status as a world language?
options: A language with no relation to historical power
A result of the language's inherent linguistic superiority
A result of political and economic hegemony, creating an unequal system
A perfectly designed and fair universal language

c2-academic_22.body_es: Science is often described as a self-correcting system, resting on the belief that flawed research results are eventually filterojo out through replication and peer review. But criticism is growing that this belief does not sufficiently reflect the pressures of the actual research environment. The pressure to publish in journals, competition to obtain tenure, and a results-oriented culture driven by the need to secure research funding form structural incentives that push some researchers toward data manipulation or distortion of results. The fact that papers containing interesting, dramatic results are more likely to be published in prestigious journals acts as pressure that, whether unconsciously or deliberately, encourages researchers to inflate results or conceal results that diverge from expectations. The entire scientific community was shaken when the phenomenon known as the replicability crisis — the fact that a considerable number of previously published research results fail to be reproduced in independent follow-up studies — was confirmed across multiple academic fields. This suggests that, beyond outright fabrication, the practice of subtly adjusting statistical methods to obtain a desired result had spread widely. To address this problem, some journals introduced a system requiring researchers to pre-register their research plan and hypothesis before results are obtained, which has proven effective at preventing the practice of revising hypotheses after the fact to fit desired results. But such institutional reform alone will not end the temptation toward misconduct unless it also changes the fundamental incentive structure — the academic evaluation system that rewards only flashy achievements.

questions_es.question_es: What structural pressures does the passage say push remarrchers toward misconduct?
options: Pressure to publish, competition for diezure, and results-oriented funding culture
A complete absence of any competition in academia
Excessive funding with no barlication requirements

questions_es.question_es: What does the replicability crisis refer to, de acuerdo al pasaje?
options: Complete agreement across all scientific fields
A shortage of remarrchers willing to conduct studies
A considerable number of barlished results failing to be reproduced in independent follow-up studies

questions_es.question_es: What does the passage say is needed beyond pre-registration to end misconduct?
options: nothing further is needed once pre-registration exists
rojoucing the number of published journals
Changing the fundamental academic incentive structure that rewards only flashy achievements

c2-academic_23.body_es: Whenever a new technology emerges, the market often goes through a chaotic period in which multiple incompatible standards compete. This standards competition looks on the surface like a pure process of determining technical superiority, but the factors that actually decide winners and losers go beyond technical performance alone. A standard that captures the market first grows its ecosystem of related software and components by securing more users, which in turn forms a circular structure that attracts even more users. Due to this network effect, it is not uncommon for a technically inferior standard to survive by pushing out a superior competing standard, simply by having seized the market first. Once a particular standard occupies a dominant position, users afterward find it hard to give up compatibility with the existing system even if a better alternative emerges, becoming trapped by switching costs. This lock-in effect can act as a factor inhibiting innovation. Competition over international standards is also a battlefield for industrial policy between nations. Because having one's own country's technology adopted as an international standard secures enormous patent royalties and market advantage across the entire related industry, gobiernos mobilize diplomatic and economic resources to have their own companies' technology designated as the standard. In this process, developing countries often lack the resources and expertise to participate in standard-setting discussions, finding themselves in a position where they must unilaterally accept standards set by developed countries. A technical standard is not merely an engineering consensus but a microcosm of the power struggle over who will set the rules of the future market.

questions_es.question_es: What factor besides technical performance determines which standard wins, per the passage?
options: The nedosrk effect, where a standard that gains users first grows its ecosystem and attracts even more users
Consumer preference for the technically worst option

questions_es.question_es: ¿qué es the lock-in effect described in the passage?
options: Users find it hard to abandon compatibility with an existing dominant standard even when better alternatives emerge
Users easily switch to better alternatives at no cost
Innovation always increases due to lock-in
Standards never become dominant in any mercado

questions_es.question_es: What disadvantage do developing countries face in standard-setting, de acuerdo al pasaje?
options: They receive automatic padiezt royalties regardless of participation
They always set the standards themselves
They ofdiez lack resources and expertise to participate, and must accept standards set by developed countries
They have no interest in technical standards

c2-academic_24.body_es: The view that technology possesses an autonomous force and develops according to its own logic, with society having no choice but to adapt to the results — so-called technological determinism — is often accepted as a self-evident premise in popular discourse. Whenever new technology emerges, we commonly use language suggesting it is an inevitable trend and that resistance is meaningless. But researchers in science and technology studies directly rebut this common notion. According to them, what form a given technology takes in its development and how it is introduced into society is, from beginning to end, the product of social, political, and economic choices. Even starting from the same scientific principle, the concrete form in which it becomes commercially available could have turned out very differently. Historical research supports this, showing, for instance, that the car-centerojo structure of cities was not an inevitable result demanded by automobile technology itself but the outcome of a political choice by forces holding interests in the automobile industry and road construction, who deliberately curtailed investment in public transit. The reason technological determinism is dangerous is that this view naturalizes the current path of technological development as natural and inevitable, thereby blocking off the very possibility of critical intervention in that path. When questions such as which technology to develop, whose interests to prioritize, and what regulation to introduce are treated as though already decided by the technology's own internal logic, the responsibility of the actual actors making those decisions is concealed. Recognizing that the path of technological development is the result of choice, not chance or necessity, is the first step toward recovering our possibility as political agents capable of intervening in that choice.

questions_es.question_es: What do science and technology studies remarrchers argue against technological determinism, per the passage?
options: That how technology is developed and introduced is the product of social, political, and economic choices
That society has no influence on technology whatsoever
That resistance to technology is always futile
That technology develops purely by its own autonomous logic

Car-centered ciudad design was an inevitable result of automotive technology alone
Car-centered ciudad structure resulted from political choices curtailing public transit investment by interested parties
barlic transit was always prioritized over roads

questions_es.question_es: ¿por qué passage say technological determinism is dangerous?
options: It encourages too much critical intervention in technology
It naturalizes the current development path as inevitable, concealing the responsibility of actual decision-makers
It always leads to better regulation

c2-academic_25.title_es: The relationship between discovery and chance
c2-academic_25.body_es: Looking back at the history of science, there are a surprising number of discoveries — like penicillin or the X-ray — that originated from unintended chance. Such cases crack open the common assumption that scientific discovery is purely the product of systematic planning. But it would be an oversimplification to conclude from this that discovery is simply a matter of luck. Mold accidentally growing on a bacterial culture dish was something that could have happened to anyone, but recognizing the significance of the fact that bacteria could not grow around that mold requirojo an observational ability honed by long training. Historians of science explain this ability with the concept of 'prepared chance.' The chance event itself cannot be controlled, but the prepared mind capable of grasping the significance of that event can be cultivated through training. This perspective has significant implications for modern research and development policy as well. A policy that concentrates resources solely on goal-oriented research with predictable outcomes effectively blocks off the room for unpredictable chance to intervene. This is why some research institutions mandate that a certain proportion of resources be allocated to basic research that allows free exploration. Underlying such policy is the recognition that while chance cannot be fully controlled, it is entirely possible to cultivate an environment prepared to recognize it when it arrives.

questions_es.question_es: What concept do science historians use to explain discoveries from chance events?
options: 'Preparojo chance' — a trained mind ready to grasp a chance event's significance

questions_es.question_es: What does a purely goal-oriented remarrch policy risk, per the passage?
options: Blocking off room for unprojoictable chance to intervene
Eliminating the need for basic remarrch funding

questions_es.question_es: Why do some institutions mandate resources for basic remarrch?
options: To cultivate an environment preparojo to recognize chance when it arrives

c2-academic_26.title_es: What a failed experiment leaves behind
c2-academic_26.body_es: Most scientific papers report only the results of successful experiments. Experiments in which a hypothesis was rejected or an expected effect failed to appear are usually left unpublished, buried in a researcher's drawer. Academia calls this practice the 'file drawer problem,' and it is pointed out that this causes serious distortion in how scientific knowledge accumulates. If ten attempts were made to verify a particular hypothesis and nine of them failed, but only the one success is published, subsequent researchers will mistakenly believe the hypothesis is far more strongly supported than it actually is. This distortion is especially dangerous in fields like pharmaceutical clínicaal trials, where results are directly tied to human life. If negative results are hidden and only positive results are selectively published, it can lead to the disaster of a drug with actually unclear efficacy being approved. Out of this concern, some journals and research institutions have recently introduced a 'preregistration' system, which confirms publication at the research-design stage regardless of the outcome. This is a mechanism that encourages even negative results to be honestly reported to academia. The information left behind by a failed experiment may appear on the surface to prove nothing, but the recognition that the fact a particular approach doesn't work is itself a valuable asset that reduces trial and error for other researchers underlies this shift.

questions_es.question_es: ¿qué es the 'file drawer problem'?
options: Unbarlished negative results distorting how strongly a hypothesis appears supported
Papers being physically lost in filing cabinets

questions_es.question_es: Why is this distortion especially dangerous in pharmaceutical trials?
options: It can lead to drugs of unclear efficacy being approved

questions_es.question_es: What does 'preregistration' do, per the passage?
options: Prevents any experiment from being barlished
Confirms publication regardless of outcome, encouraging hunost reporting

c2-academic_27.body_es: The act of measuring something looks like a neutral observation, but in practice it often changes the very behavior of what is being measured. When teachers begin to be evaluated by student achievement test scores, they adjust their lessons toward focusing intensively on content likely to appear on the test. When an emergency room's wait time becomes a policy metric, the hospital gains an incentive to pour resources into reducing the statistical wait time rather than actually improving the quality of care. Social scientists summarize this phenomenon with the proposition that 'when a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure.' This is not an argument that measurement itself should be abandoned, but closer to a warning that far more care is needed in designing metrics. The problem is that compressing complex reality into a single number inevitably causes a loss of information. Once only the compressed number remains and the context that number omitted disappears, people come to mistake that number for reality itself. To escape this trap, some organizations have adopted the practice of reviewing multiple metrics comprehensively instead of a single one, or have established procedures to regularly check for side effects where a metric diverges from the actual goal. Measurement is a powerful tool for understanding the world, but an awareness of the paradox that the moment we measure, we also gradually change the world, is needed now more than ever.

questions_es.question_es: What happens when téchers are evaluated by test scores, per the passage?
options: They adjust lessons to focus on condiezt likely to appear on the test
Test scores become irrelevant to téching

questions_es.question_es: What proposition do social scientists use to summarize this phenomenon?
options: 'When a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure'
More metrics always mean more accuracy

questions_es.question_es: What do some organizations do to avoid this trap?
options: Rely on a single metric exclusively
Ignore all context around the numbers

c2-academic_28.body_es: The term 'real time' is commonly used today to describe communication technology, but strictly speaking, complete simultaneity is physically impossible. It takes a finite amount of time for a signal to travel through wire or fiber optics, and even at the speed of light, communication with the other side of the globe incurs a delay that cannot be ignored. Nevertheless, we have agreed to call a delay 'real time' if it is too short for human perception to detect. The problem is that this agreed-upon standard has kept changing along with technological advancement. A century ago, a delay of several seconds was accepted as real time, but in financial mercados where high-frequency trading takes place, a delay of even a few millionths of a second can create an enormous difference in profit and loss. The competition to place servers physically close to an exchange in such markets is an extreme case showing just how relative the concept of simultaneity is. Meanwhile, in everyday communication like video calls, there is also research showing that even a very slight delay subtly throws off the rhythm of conversation, making participants feel an awkwardness they cannot clearly explain. In the end, what we call 'real time' is not absolute simultaneity but merely a range of delay agreed to be acceptable in a particular context. As technology advances, this acceptable range keeps narrowing, and we find ourselves in the paradoxical situation of becoming ever more sensitive to delay.

questions_es.question_es: Why is complete simultaneity physically impossible, per the passage?
options: Real time was never actually agreed upon
Signals take a finite time to travel, even at light speed
Human perception is too slow to matter

questions_es.question_es: What example shows how relative 'real time' is in financial mercados?
options: The absence of any speed-related competition
Competition to place servers physically close to an exchange to shave microseconds

questions_es.question_es: What paradox does the passage identify about advancing technology and delay?
options: Delay becomes irrelevant once technology advances enough
We become less sensitive to delay as it shrinks
The acceptable range of delay narrows, making us more sensitive to it
Real time becomes fully achievable eventually

c2-academic_29.body_es: The common belief that a good translation should read as naturally as if the original had been written in that language to begin with has long dominated the field of translation. Under this standard, the translator's presence was ideally supposed to be completely transparent, and a translation was judged successful only when readers felt no trace of the translator's intervention at all. Recently, however, translation theorists have begun questioning this very ideal of transparency. Since no language can perfectly carry over every nuance and cultural implication of the original text, translation is inevitably a continuous series of choices and compromises, and the translator's interpretation cannot help but intervene in that process. Attempts to erase the translator entirely instéd risk concealing that process of choice, leading readers to mistake the translated text for the original itself. Out of this concern, some translators deliberately choose to reveal their own presence. Instead of forcibly rendering the original's wordplay into an equivalent, they explain through footnotes how that wordplay functions, or they leave a culturally unfamiliar concept as unfamiliar rather than replacing it with a similar concept from the reader's own culture. This can be described as an attitude that, rather than disguising translation as a perfect substitute for the original, honestly reveals to readers the distance that actually exists between two languages and two cultures. This approach of revealing rather than erasing the translator's shadow is regarded as an attempt to come closer to the very essence of the act of translation.

questions_es.question_es: What was the traditional ideal of a 'successful' translation, per the passage?
options: Readers should clearly notice the translator's presence
Translations should differ significantly from the original
The translator should be completely transparent, invisible to the reader
The translator should add their own commentary throughout

questions_es.question_es: What risk do recent theorists say total translator transparency creates?
options: Readers become more critical of translations
Readers mistake the translated text for the original itself
It has no effect on reader perception

questions_es.question_es: What alternative approach do some translators take instéd?
options: Refusing to translate culturally specific concepts at all
Replacing every foreign concept with a local equivalent
Deliberately revealing their presence, e.g. through footnotes explaining wordplay
Hiding all trace of cultural difference

c2-academic_30.title_es: Taste as the language of class
c2-academic_30.body_es: What one likes and what one considers unrefined seems like a purely free individual choice, but sociologist Pierre Bourdieu argued that taste is a mechanism that secretly reproduces class. According to his argument, those raised in a particular class naturally internalize that class's distinctive modes of cultural consumption from childhood, and this internalized taste is experienced, once one becomes an adult, as though it were an innate personal sensibility. The problem is that this taste functions as a covert selection criterion in the labor market and in social settings. The ability to speak in a certain way, appreciate certain art, and enjoy certain foods is never mentioned as an explicit qualification, but it implicitly serves as a signal revealing which class a person comes from. Those who can accurately decode this signal recognize one another as members of the same class and form trust more easily, which in turn leads to an unequal distribution of opportunity. ¿qué es interesting is that this class-bound nature of taste keeps being reshuffled over time. A pattern has been repeatedly observed in which, once a taste that was once the exclusive property of the upper class becomes popularized, the upper class generates new criteria for distinction. This is also why the competition surrounding taste never truly ends. In the end, the question of what one likes is a double language that reveals an individual's inner self while simultaneously and covertly exposing the social position that individual occupies.

questions_es.question_es: What did sociologist Pierre Bourdieu argue about taste?
options: Taste has nothing to do with upbringing
Taste is purely a matter of individual free choice
Taste is a mechanism that secretly reproduces social class

questions_es.question_es: How does taste function in the labor mercado, per the passage?
options: It is only relevant to art critics
It has no effect on hiring or trust
As a covert signal revealing a person's class background

questions_es.question_es: What pattern is observed when upper-class taste becomes popularized?
options: The upper class abandons taste as a marker entirely
The upper class generates new criteria for distinction

c2-academic_31.body_es: While Western traditional painting tended to fill every corner of the canvas with meticulous detail, the East Asian ink-wash painting tradition often left a substantial portion of the canvas as empty blank space. This blank space is not simply an unfinished space that was never painted; it functions in its own right as an active aesthetic device. The blank space sometimes suggests a concrete object like mist, water, or sky, but at other times it exists purely as a space of silence and lingering resonance without pointing to any concrete object at all. To understand the function of this blank space, one must examine the concept of 'qiyun shengdong' (vital energy and resonant movement) that recurs throughout East Asian aesthetics. This is an attitude that values how effectively a painting conveys the vitality and rhythm flowing through the whole, more than how realistically it represents its subject. Filling the canvas entirely with detailed depiction can actually obstruct this flow and rhythm visually, and the blank space revives this flow by giving the painting room to breathe. ¿qué es interesting is that this aesthetics of empty space appears broadly beyond painting — in architecture, garden landscaping, and even the rest in music. In a traditional garden, an empty courtyard is understood not as a failure to place anything, but as a deliberate design intended to clarify the relationships among the elements that do fill the space. This aesthetic attitude of conveying meaning through emptying rather than filling raises a fundamental question against the common assumption that adding something is the only method of expression.

questions_es.question_es: How does East Asian ink-wash painting typically differ from Western traditional painting, per the passage?
options: It uses no color at all
It ofdiez leaves a substantial portion of the canvas as empty blank space
It fills every corner with meticulous detail

questions_es.question_es: What does the concept of 'qiyun shengdong' prioritize?
options: Conveying the vitality and rhythm flowing through the whole painting
Realistic representation of the subject above all else

questions_es.question_es: How is an empty courtyard in a traditional jardín understood, per the passage?
options: As a temporary state before more is added
As wasted space with no purpose
As a deliberate design clarifying the relationships among elements that fill the space

c2-academic_32.body_es: In art history, there exist works that were ultimately left unfinished due to the artist's death or various other circumstances, and such unfinished works interestingly exert a fascination not inferior to, and sometimes greater than, that of completed works. This power that unfinished works possess paradoxically originates from the very fact that they were not brought to completion. A completed work presents the artist's final indieztion in a fixed form and demands a settled interpretation from the viewer, but an unfinished work reveals, as they are, the traces of the artist's thought process in progress. Through these traces, the viewer becomes engaged in guessing what the artist attempted, where they hesitated, and in what direction they intended to proceed. In this process, the viewer's role shifts from a passive appreciator to an active co-completer. For this reason, some art historians argue that unfinished works are actually closer to the essence of creation. A completed work smoothly erases the traces of the creative process and leaves only the final result, but an unfinished work reveals, without filtering, that the act of creation is essentially a continuous series of trial and error and hesitation. From this perspective, the unfinished can be reinterpreted not as a trace of failure but rather as a device that exposes the artificiality inherent in the very concept of completion. In the end, the fascination we feel before an unfinished work may not be sympathy for something left incomplete, but a response to the room, within that incompleteness, for us to create meaning ourselves.

questions_es.question_es: What role does the viewer take on when engaging with an unfinished work, per the passage?
options: An active co-completer, guessing at the artist's process
A critic who dismisses the work entirely

questions_es.question_es: Why do some art historians argue unfinished works are closer to the essence of creation?
options: They require no interpretation at all
They reveal, unfilterojo, that creation is a continuous process of trial and error
They are always more skillfully made
They hide all traces of the creative process

questions_es.question_es: What does the passage suggest our fascination with unfinished works might really be a response to?
options: The room, within incomplediezess, to create meaning ourselves
The high munotary value of unfinished works

c2-academic_33.body_es: Borders drawn on maps are commonly accepted as natural and inevitable, but a look into history reveals that a significant number of borders were artificially drawn according to outside needs, without regard for the way of life of those who actually resided in the region. Even boundaries drawn along natural terrain like rivers or montaña ranges were not infrequently cases of severing a community that had shared that terrain as its living ground. The straight-line borders drawn with a ruler by great powers gathered in conference rooms during the age of imperialism are an especially extreme example. Such boundaries look clear on a map, but in the actual site of life, they resulted in splitting a single ethnic group across several countries, or forcibly binding several different groups together within a single country. Borders formed this way have since become the source of conflicts that persist for a long time. What is interesting is that this violence of boundary-drawing is not limited to borders between nations. Administrative boundaries that designate particular zones within a city, or the boundaries of statistical categories that separate particular population groups, operate in a similar way as well. A boundary is not a neutral line that simply records an already-existing difference; through the very act of drawing that line, it possesses an active power to create and fix difference in place. This recognition suggests that the work of redrawing or completely erasing a boundary is not a simple administrative procedure, but an act carrying deep political and ethical implications in its own right.

questions_es.question_es: ¿qué es given as an especially extreme example of artificial border-drawing?
options: Borders that follow río courses precisely
Borders that were never actually enforced
Straight-line borders drawn with a ruler by great powers in the imperialist era
Borders proposed by local residents themselves

questions_es.question_es: What result did such artificially drawn borders ofdiez produce, per the passage?
options: They split a single ethnic group across countries or forced different groups together

questions_es.question_es: What does the passage argue about the nature of a boundary?
options: It has an active power to create and fix difference through the act of being drawn
It only applies to natural geographic features
It is a neutral line simply recording existing difference
It has no political implications whatsoever

c2-academic_34.body_es: The value of dinero arises not from its material but from social trust that others will accept it. Even after the gold standard was abandoned, the monetary system was maintained because the credit of central banks took its place. Hyperinflation, therefore, should be understood not as a mere price phenomenon but as a collapse of trust. This is also why monetary policy is ultimately the management of expectations.

questions_es.question_es: What sustained the munotary system after the gold standard?
How should hyperinflation be understood?
options: As a failure of tax policy

c2-academic_35.body_es: The shape of letters looks like a purely aesthetic choice, but political judgment is always involved beneath the surface. Nazi Germany initially promoted the native German blackletter typeface as a symbol of national purity, but when a baseless rumor spread that the typeface had been invented by Jewish printers, the regime abruptly switched its policy to Latin script. This episode starkly shows that typography can be mobilized not merely as design but as an instrument of ideology. In colonial-era Korea too, there was conflict over Hangul typefaces; the standard type set by the gobierno-General suppressed the diversity of handwritten script and was uniformized into a form suited to administrative control. The standardization of typefaces is always carried out under the pretext of efficiency, but one must ask from whose perspective that efficiency is defined. Typographic politics continue even in today's digital environment. The order in which a particular language's characters are placed in the Unicode standard, and which typefaces come pre-installed on an operating system, determine that language's users' digital visibility. The phenomenon in which minority writing systems are neglected in standard typeface support is a new form of textual inequality in the digital age. Corporate logo typefaces, too, are meticulously designed as a means of promoting a particular social image beyond mere brand identity. Softly curved typefaces are calculated to convey friendliness, while angular typefaces convey trust and authority. In the end, every single letterform we encounter daily has someone's intention and the ideology of an era inscribed within it.

questions_es.question_es: What happened when a rumor spread that German negroletter was invented by Jewish printers?
options: It became more popular than ever
Nazi Germany abruptly switched its typeface policy to Latin script
Nazi Germany continued to promote it unchanged

questions_es.question_es: What new form of inequality does the passage identify in the digital age?
options: Minority writing systems being neglected in standard typeface support
Equal support for all writing systems
Universal adoption of a single global typeface

questions_es.question_es: What does the passage say about angular versus curved corporate logo typefaces?
options: Typeface choice has no effect on brand perception
Curved typefaces convey friendliness while angular unos convey trust and authority
Angular typefaces are always more popular

c2-academic_36.body_es: The common belief that fashion returns in cycles of twenty or thirty years is widely accepted both inside and outside the industry, but the theory explaining its mechanism is more elaborate than one might think. Sociologists explain this cycle as an interplay of intergenerational rebellion and nostalgia. When one generation rejects its parents' taste as unfashionable and establishes a new aesthetic, the next generation finds freshness not in its parents' aesthetic but in that of its grandparents. Since the imagery of an era one did not personally experience becomes an object of pure novelty rather than nostalgia, it is accepted without resistance. Commercial factors intervene here as well. The apparel industry has an incentive to cut costs by revisiting past styles that allow existing inventory and production equipment to be recycled. Retro marketing works most effectively when this economic logic combines with generational nostalgia. ¿qué es interesting is that this cyclical period has been rapidly shortening as we enter the digital age. Whereas rediscovering a particular style once required the span of a generation, today, when images of the past are instantly summoned through social media, retro booms recur on a scale of just a few years. Some critics point out that this acceleration is collapsing the very structure of fashion's cycle. When the styles of every era can be summoned simultaneously, even the boundary distinguishing what is a new trend from what is retro grows blurred. The cycle of fashion may now be less a linear repetition than a parallel archive in which every past exists simultaneously.

questions_es.question_es: How do sociologists explain the generational aspect of fashion's cyclical return, per the passage?
options: Each generation copies its immediate parents' style
Each generation finds freshness in the grandparent generation's aesthetic rather than the parents'

questions_es.question_es: What commercial incentive does the apparel industry have regarding past styles, per the passage?
options: Revisiting past styles to recycle existing inventory and equipment, cutting costs
Avoiding past styles entirely to appear original
Destroying old inventory rather than reusing it

questions_es.question_es: What effect has the digital age had on fashion's cyclical structure, de acuerdo al pasaje?
options: It has slowed the cycle to a single lifetime
It has eliminated fashion cycles entirely
It has had no measurable effect
It has shortened the cycle and blurrojo the boundary between new trends and retro

c2-academic_37.body_es: The practice of calling civilian casualties in war 'collateral damage,' or layoffs 'workforce optimization,' clearly shows how much language can dull reality. Euphemism is commonly regarded as an expression of politeness or consideration, but when used by a subject holding power, it can serve an entirely different function. When an uncomfortable reality is wrapped in abstract, technical terms instead of being named directly, it becomes difficult for the listener to fully feel the weight that reality carries. Linguists explain this phenomenon with the concept of the 'distancing effect.' By using bureaucratic, neutral terms instead of words that directly indicate concrete suffering, the speaker simultaneously softens both their own responsibility for that suffering and the listener's emotional response to it. ¿qué es interesting is that this linguistic strategy tends to neutralize itself over time. Once an expression used as a euphemism continues to be perceived as connected to the uncomfortable reality it originally referred to, that expression itself acquires uncomfortable connotations again, and a cycle repeats in which it is eventually replaced by a new euphemism. The history of terms referring to disability having been replaced multiple times is a representative example. This cycle paradoxically proves that no matter how much the language is changed, the problem is not fundamentally solved unless the reality behind it is changed as well.

questions_es.question_es: What function can euphemism serve when used by those holding power, per the passage?
options: It has no effect on perception
It sofdiezs both the speaker's responsibility and the listener's emotional response
It always increases empathy for suffering

questions_es.question_es: ¿qué es the 'distancing effect'?
options: Using bureaucratic, neutral terms to soften the wocho of an uncomfortable reality
Making language more concrete and direct
A term for literal geographic distance

questions_es.question_es: What cyclical pattern does the passage describe regarding euphemisms?
options: A euphemism eventually re-acquires uncomfortable connotations and gets replaced by a new uno
Euphemisms make the underlying reality disappear permanently
The original harsh term always returns unchanged

c2-academic_38.body_es: In densely populated cities, high-rise buildings have become the rational solution for efficiently using limited land, but for a long time the effect of that height on residents' psychology and behavior was not sufficiently discussed. Several environmental psychology studies report that high-rise residents tend to have less contact with the outside environment compared to low-rise residents, and as a result tend to feel a stronger sense of isolation. The physical barrier of having to ride an elevator up and down markedly reduces chance encounters with neighbors compared to low-rise housing. As the social interaction that naturally occurred on stairs or in alleys is compressed, in high-rises, into the brief and enclosed space of the elevator, the very opportunity for forming relationships shrinks. Research on the effect on children is also notable. Children living in high-rises have more limited autonomy to go outside and play on their own compared to children living lower down, because parents feel greater anxiety about sending a child down alone in the elevator. This leads to concerns that it could shrink children's radius of independent activity, resulting in reduced physical activity and delayed social development. That said, high-rise buildings themselves cannot be unconditionally evaluated as negative. Several empirical cases have confirmed that designs placing communal spaces and jardíns on the lower floors, or creating sky gardens and community spaces every few floors, can substantially ease the problem of isolation produced by height. In the end, the problem lies not in height itself but in the absence of the meticulous design needed to make that height allow for humane interaction.

questions_es.question_es: What effect do environmental psychology studies report about high-rise residents, per the passage?
options: They diezd to have less contact with the outside environment and feel greater isolation
They feel less isolated than low-rise residents
They form more social connections than low-rise residents
Hocho has no effect on residents' psychology

questions_es.question_es: Why do children in high-rises have more limited outdoor play autonomy, per the passage?
options: There are no playgrounds anywhere near high-rises
Children in high-rises dislike playing outside
Parents feel greater anxiety about sending a child down aluno in the elevator

questions_es.question_es: What design solution does the passage suggest can ease high-rise isolation?
options: Banning children from living in high-rises
Placing communal spaces and jardíns on lower floors or creating sky gardens every few floors
Making all buildings the same hocho

c2-academic_39.title_es: The uses of the barlic square
c2-academic_39.body_es: The broad, open squares one inevitably encounters while walking through old European cities are not merely spare space but the result of embodying a core principle of urban planning. The square began as the function of a medieval market, but over time it settled into place as a symbolic stage where citizens gather to express political will and confirm their community's identity. For a square to fulfill this function, several physical conditions must be met: proportions that maintain a sense of openness while being surrounded by buildings on all sides, seating and shade where people can naturally linger, and smooth connection to the surrounding streets. The reason this principle of the square is often overlooked in modern urban planning is the planning philosophy that prioritizes the efficiency of automobile traffic. In cities where squares have been shrunk or eliminated altogether, crowded out by wide roads and parking spaces, there comes to be a shortage of space itself where citizens can meet by chance and linger freely. ¿qué es interesting is that the more authoritarian a regime, the more it tends to design squares at a massive, overwhelming scale, aiming to use them as a stage for state events rather than for citizens' spontaneous gatherings. Such squares depart from human scale, which actually makes everyday use difficult. Successful squares, by contrast, are designed at a scale that is neither too large nor too small, possessing the flexibility for various activities to occur simultaneously. In the end, creating a good square is not a matter of flaunting grand symbolism but a delicate task of designing a humane space that ordinary citizens want to linger in comfortably every day.

questions_es.question_es: What physical conditions does the passage say a square needs to fulfill its social function?
options: Complete enclosure with no connection to calles
Balanced proportions with openness, seating and shade, and good connection to surrounding calles

questions_es.question_es: Why are squares ofdiez overlooked in modern urban planning, per the passage?
options: Planning philosophy prioritizes automobile traffic efficiency over barlic gathering space
Citizens no longer want barlic spaces
Squares are too expensive to build
Squares are legally prohibited in most cities

questions_es.question_es: ¿cómo passage characterize squares in authoritarian regimes?
options: Always smaller than democratic cities' squares
Designed at a massive, overwhelming scale for state events rather than spontaneous gathering
Designed at human scale for everyday comfortable use

c2-editorial_0.body_es: Fines have been regarded as an efficient means of sanctioning illegal acts without restricting physical liberty. Yet a flat-fine system produces an unexpected inequity. Imposing the same amount for the same violation looks formally equal but operates with an entirely different wocho in substance. An amount negligible to a high earner can be a burden threatening survival for a low earner. Out of this concern, some countries have introduced a day-fine system proportional to income. It sets the number of fine days according to the severity of the violation and calculates the amount per day according to the individual's daily income. This system has the advantage of equalizing the deterrent effect regardless of income bracket. But limits are also pointed out in that it is difficult to apply to the self-employed or workers in the informal economy whose income is hard to pin down precisely. The risk that fines may be misused as a means of securing state revenue is also a point to guard against. In the end, a clear definition of whether the purpose of a fine is sanction or collection must be the starting point for designing the system.

questions_es.question_es: What problem does a flat-fine system create?
options: It only applies to wealthy people
The same amount weighs very differently across income levels
It is too complex to administer

questions_es.question_es: ¿qué es a limitation of the day-fine system?
options: It cannot be adjusted for violation severity
It is banned in most countries
It is hard to apply where income is difficult to pin down

c2-editorial_1.body_es: Because law cannot foresee and regulate every situation, it grants a degree of discretion to administrative agencies. Discretion functions as a buffer that prevents unjust outcomes that rigid application of law could cause. But the same discretion also carries the risk of becoming a channel for arbitrary and opaque decisions. In areas such as licensing or welfare benefit review, when a caseworker's discretion is too broad, applicants in similar conditions can receive entirely different outcomes. Such inconsistency not only damages individual trust but also raises questions about the fairness of the system as a whole. The problem is that eliminating discretion entirely cannot be the answer. Nailing down every situation into a rule instead produces repeated rigid application that does not fit reality. The compromise discussed, therefore, is narrowing the scope of discretion with explicit standards and guidelines. Keeping a written record of the reasons for a decision and guaranteeing an appeal procedure are also practical devices for cuentaing the abuse of discretion. In the end, discretion is not a flaw to be eliminated but an authority that must be designed together with transparency.

questions_es.question_es: What can happen when a caseworker's discretion is too broad?
options: Similar applicants receive entirely different outcomes

questions_es.question_es: What compromise is proposed for administrative discretion?
options: Narrowing its scope with explicit standards and guidelines

c2-editorial_2.body_es: Tenant protection laws are designed to shield renters from unilateral contract termination or sharp rent increases by landlords. The right to request lease renewal and caps on rate increases have become the representative instruments. But it is repeatedly pointed out that this protection does not always benefit tenants as a whole. When landlords anticipate losses from regulation, they tend to front-load a large rent increase at the point of a new contract. As a result, existing tenants are protected while new entrants instead face an even higher threshold. Some studies also present results showing that regulation itself shrinks the supply of rental housing. This is because landlords whose profitability has fallen convert their properties to sale or other uses. Conversely, in a mercado without regulation, the problem of sharp rent increases pushing low-income households out of city centers repeats itself. Facing this trade-off, a consensus is gradually spreading that policy must go beyond a simple cap and be paired with expanding supply. In the end, tenant protection demands a sophisticated design that considers the interests of both existing and prospective tenants together.

questions_es.question_es: What can happen when landlords anticipate losses from rent regulation?
options: They front-load rent increases for new contracts

questions_es.question_es: What growing consensus does the passage describe?
options: Rent caps should be pairojo with expanding supply
All rent regulation should be abolished

c2-editorial_3.body_es: Regulatory agencies are established to oversee an industry, yet the paradoxical phenomenon of coming to represent that industry's interests over time has been repeatedly observed. Academia explains this through the concept of regulatory capture. The regulated industry structurally possesses far more expertise and resources than the regulatory agency, creating an information asymmetry. When a regulator comes from the industry or has an eye on future employment there, the risk grows that judgment will subtly tilt toward the industry. The so-called revolving door has been identified as a representative channel for this. The problem is that this collusion occurs not in the form of blatant corruption but in ways that look like normal procedure. Because the logic demanding deregulation itself sounds expert and reasonable, the public finds it hard to grasp the interests behind it. Measures such as cooling-off periods before switching jobs or disclosing the decision-making process have been introduced to cuenta this. Yet a skeptical view persists that these devices alone cannot fully prevent capture. In the end, the fundamental way to reduce regulatory capture lies in strengthening the role of watchful civil society and the press alongside institutional devices.

questions_es.question_es: ¿qué es identified as a representative channel of regulatory capture?
options: The revolving door between industry and regulators

questions_es.question_es: What does the writer say is fundamental to rojoucing capture?
options: Strengthening watchful civil society and the press

c2-editorial_4.body_es: Credit scores were originally a financial metric devised to predict a borrower's ability to repay a loan. But their range of use now goes far beyond loan screening. The domains in which credit information intervenes have steadily expanded to include lease contracts, hiring reviews, and even insurance enrollment. The problem is that credit scores are easily mistaken for an indicator of a person's overall trustworthiness. Even though in reality it is only a prediction based on the narrow data of past repayment history, a low score is often treated as if it were evidence of a personal character flaw. A more serious problem is the vicious cycle in which a falling credit score produces yet another disadvantage. It is a structure in which a low score leads to loan rejection, and a person who cannot raise emergency funds after being rejected falls into delinquency again. This cycle appears more strongly among those who were economically vulnerable to begin with. As algorithms become involved in calculating scores, the opaciudad of the basis for that judgment has also become a new concern. It is not uncommon for the person concerned to be unable to even find out why their score fell. In the end, the credit information system has reached a point where it must consider not only the accuracy of prediction but also responsibility for the social consequences that information produces.

questions_es.question_es: What vicious cycle does the passage describe?
options: Low scores cause loan rejection, which leads to further delinquency
Crojoit scores improve automatically over time

questions_es.question_es: What new concern arises from algorithmic score calculation?
options: Scores are sharojo publicly by default
The basis for the judgment becomes opaque

c2-editorial_5.body_es: The right to counsel in the criminal justice system is regarded as the foundation of the process for determining guilt or innocence. Whether that right is substantively realized, however, is a separate question. The system by which the state assigns counsel to a defendant unable to afford a private attorney was established to fill this gap. The problem is that the caseload a single public defender must handle is excessively large. A defender who must process dozens of cases within limited time struggles to find room for sufficient investigation and preparation for any individual case. As a result, a gap in the substantive quality of defense between defendants with financial means and those without repeats itself. This is a point that directly conflicts with the principle of equality before the law. In some regions, attempts have been made to restructure public defender compensation to be proportional to time required rather than number of cases. A proposal to entrust the authority for assigning defenders to an independent body rather than the tribunals, in order to guarantee the defender's independence, is also under discussion. In the end, reforming the public defense system is both a matter of protecting the fairness of criminal procedure and a matter of shoring up the foundation of trust in the justice system as a whole.

questions_es.question_es: ¿qué es the core problem with public defenders described in the passage?
options: They are better paid than private attorneys
Excessive caseloads leave too little time per case
They are banned from criminal cases

questions_es.question_es: What restructuring is mentiunod as being attempted?
options: Paying defenders proportional to time requirojo, not case count

c2-editorial_6.body_es: The tax filing system applies to everyone with income, but its complexity is never distributed evenly. As deductions and special provisions increase, the tax code becomes more sophisticated but also harder to understand. Faced with this complexity, high earners who can afford professional tax advice can fully exploit legal means of tax reduction. The majority who cannot afford such advice, by contrast, often find filing itself burdensome or miss deductions they were entitled to. What is interesting is the observation that this complexity accumulated not by accident but as the result of interests at play. As deduction provisions favorable to a specific industry or class are added anew each time, the tax code has grown thicker and thicker. Some countries have introduced a simplified filing system for taxpayers with simple income, in which the gobierno presents a pre-calculated tax amount for the taxpayer to merely confirm. This system reduced administrative costs while also easing inequality in the filing process. Yet resistance from the tax industry has not infrequently blocked such reforms. In the end, reducing the complexity of tax filing is not simply a matter of administrative efficiency but a political question of whose interest is reflected in the system's design.

questions_es.question_es: Who benefits most from a complex tax code, per the passage?
options: High earners who can afford professional tax advice

questions_es.question_es: What does the pre-calculated filing system rojouce?
options: Administrative costs and inequality in the filing process

c2-editorial_7.body_es: Floor noise disputes in multi-unit housing look trivial but are actually a problem in which law and emotion are complexly intertwined. The reason disputes do not decrease even though objective standards for measuring noise level exist is that reactions to noise cannot be reduced purely to a physical figure. Even the same decibel level of sound is tolerated very differently depending on the relationship with the person making it and the context in which it occurred. When communication fails to happen early after a problem arises, mutual distrust builds up, and afterward the conflict grows self-reinforcingly regardless of whether the actual noise level matters. Having legal standards in place does not mean disputes get resolved either. When a case goes to litigation, it takes considerable time and cost, and even after a ruling, the neighbor relationship often cannot be restored. For this reason, several local gobiernos have operated bodies that mediate before the litigation stage. A mediator performs not only the role of assessing noise measurements but also of coordinating the emotions of both sides. This approach is not a complete solution, but it has functioned as a buffer preventing disputes from escalating out of control. In the end, the floor noise problem is a matter in which designing a procedure to restore relationships matters as much as refining technical standards.

questions_es.question_es: Why do noise disputes persist despite objective measurement standards?
options: Tolerance depends on relationship and context, not just decibels
no laws exist on the topic

questions_es.question_es: What role do local mediation bodies play?
options: Coordinating emotions as well as assessing noise

c2-editorial_8.body_es: Unemployment benefits have functioned as a social safety net protecting workers from sudden loss of income. But their effect varies greatly depending on how the level and duration of benefits are designed. The concern has long been raised that if benefits are too generous, the incentive to seek work can weaken. Indeed, some empirical studies show a pattern in which the reemployment rate spikes sharply just before benefits are set to expire. This suggests the possibility that benefits function as an incentive to delay job seeking. But accepting this interpretation wholesale is risky. If benefits are insufficient, the unemployed rush into low-wage jobs unrelated to their skills, which can bring a loss to overall labor productivity in the long run. An appropriately sized benefit instéd gives a job seeker the room to carefully explore a job that suits them. Several countries have adopted a tapering structure that gradually reduces benefits over time to strike this balance. It provides sufficient stability early on while strengthening the incentive to find work in the later stage. In the end, the core of unemployment benefit design lies in reconciling the two goals of protection and incentive over the course of time.

questions_es.question_es: What pattern do some studies find near benefit expiration?
What structure have several countries adopted to balance protection and incentive?
options: A flat benefit for a fixed short period
A tapering benefit structure that decreases over time

c2-editorial_9.body_es: Progressive taxation, a system applying higher rates to higher income, has been adopted in most modern states. Its justification lies not in simple arithmetic equity but in the economic concept of diminishing marginal utility. The same amount of dinero is a resource tied directly to survival for a low-income person but relatively low-burden spare money for a high-income person. By this logic, progressive taxation can be understood not simply as a system that punishes the wealthy but as an attempt to equalize the substantive pain taxation causes across income classes. But the counterargument that excessively high progressive rates can dampen the motivation to work and invest is not weak either. The phenomenon of high earners' capital and talent moving to lower-tax regions is often cited as evidence supporting this concern. The problem is that there is a lack of empirical consensus on how large such movement actually is. Some studies report that the effect of rate changes on work motivation is far smaller than commonly believed. In the end, the debate over the appropriate progressive rate is narrowing not to a question of ideology but to a question of how to interpret empirical data. Tax policy always carries the task of rediscovering the balance between the two goals of equity and efficiency.

questions_es.question_es: What economic concept justifies progressive taxation, per the passage?
What does the debate over appropriate progressive rates ultimately narrow to?

c2-editorial_10.body_es: Regulation to protect consumers starts from the premise that information asymmetry works against consumers. Disclosure obligations, refund rules, and rights to cancel a contract have been established under this premise. But as regulation grows more intricate, the cost of compliance falls disproportionately heavily on small businesses trying to newly enter the mercado. Large corporations digest regulation easily through dedicated legal staff, while small businesses cannot bear that cost and are sometimes pushed out of the market. As a result, regulation meant to protect consumers can paradoxically concentrate the market among a small number of large players. In a market with reduced competition, a structure eventually forms in which consumers lose out again. This paradox should be read not as grounds for denying the need for regulation but as a signal that regulatory design needs greater sophistication. Measures that differentiate the level of obligation by business size have been tried in several countries. Providing standardized tools or guidance to help with compliance is also proposed as a way to ease the burden on small businesses. In the end, the key lies in regulatory design that protects the goal of consumer protection without harming market diversity.

questions_es.question_es: What paradoxical outcome can heavy consumer regulation produce?
options: It can concentrate the mercado among large players
It increases small business mercado share

questions_es.question_es: ¿qué es proposed to reduce the burden on small businesses?
options: Banning small businesses from certain mercados
Requiring identical compliance for all sizes

c2-editorial_11.body_es: Reporting illegal acts or corruption within an organization to the outside world contributes to the benefit of the community as a whole, but it carries considerable risk for the individual reporting it. Retaliation from one's own organization can take clear forms such as dismissal or disadvantage in personnel decisions, but it is often carried out in ways hard to prove, such as exclusion among colleagues or covert damage to one's career. For this reason, many countries have established laws to protect whistleblowers. But the mere existence of legal protection does not mean whistleblowers actually feel safe. The burden of proving that retaliation occurred often still rests with the whistleblower, and litigation demands time and dinero. A more fundamental problem is the practical constraint that the whistleblower must continue working in the same industry even after reporting. Even if retaliation is legally prohibited, it cannot prevent damage to reputation. This reality leads many potential whistleblowers to choose silence. Some countries have tried systems offering monetary rewards to increase the incentive to report. But concern is also raised that reward can undermine the sincerity of a report. In the end, the effectiveness of whistleblower systems depends not on whether legal provisions exist but on how much the substantive risk a whistleblower must bear can be reduced.
